text.content:
ASHES OF VELSAR

Revised adventure for four to six 1st–4th-level SW5e characters

Era: Early Imperial period, approximately three to five years after Order 66
Primary location: Bracken’s Point, Velsar
Expected length: 8–12 sessions
Advancement: Milestone
Themes: Frontier crime, community, occupation, survival, sacrifice
Variant rules: Hunted, Crueler Criticals, Wounds, Force Alignment

Adventure Summary

Velsar is an impoverished Imperial penal-resettlement world built around salvage, repair work, and low-grade industry. Its largest settlement, Bracken’s Point, has survived through generations of shared labor and stubborn independence.

The characters arrive separately after accepting work from a local fixer named Tensin Black. Their assignment appears simple: recover a stolen Imperial NaviComputer from a gang slicer before the local Rustclaws realize what they possess.

The device proves to be only one part of a larger problem.

The Rustclaws retain its military authentication wafer. Davik Renn, an aging planetary smuggler, needs the complete device to bypass an Imperial interdiction network. Meanwhile, the theft brings Commander Voss and additional Imperial forces to Velsar.

The crackdown exposes another secret: Jedi Knight Tovan Rell has lived in Velsar’s wilderness since Order 66, quietly protecting the people who once protected him.

Once the Empire confirms his presence, Velsar is no longer treated as a neglected frontier world. It becomes evidence to be erased.

Adventure Progression

ChapterCharacter LevelMilestone
Chapter 1: A Simple Job1Survive the Bent Spanner confrontation and learn about the missing authentication wafer
Chapter 2: The Rustclaw Revel2Recover the complete NaviComputer and deliver it to Davik Renn
Chapter 3: The Ghost in the Hills3Rescue Davik’s pilots, discover Tovan’s identity, and uncover Contingency Cinderglass
Chapter 4: Fire from the Sky4Escape Velsar

Characters normally complete the adventure at 4th level. Award 5th level after the epilogue when continuing into a larger campaign.

Scaling the Adventure

Use the following party-size categories throughout the module:

  • Small party: Four characters

  • Standard party: Five characters

  • Large party: Six characters

The four-character version assumes competent but not heavily optimized characters. Because Crueler Criticals and Wounds make even moderate encounters dangerous, additional enemies should usually arrive as reinforcements rather than beginning together.

General Scaling Principles

Four Characters

Use the lowest listed enemy count. Allow enemies to retreat when morale breaks. Avoid having more than one elite enemy active at 1st or 2nd level.

Five Characters

Add one ordinary enemy, improve enemy positioning, or introduce one additional encounter objective. Do not automatically add an elite enemy.

Six Characters

Add one or two ordinary enemies, preferably in separate waves. Use wider encounter spaces, crossfire, and simultaneous objectives to challenge the party without creating overwhelming opening rounds.

Reinforcement Pools

When an encounter lists reserve enemies, they do not begin on the map. One reserve group enters when:

  • An alarm is raised.

  • An enemy reaches a communications terminal.

  • The party spends several rounds in one location.

  • The current enemy group is reduced by half.

  • The encounter specifies an arrival round.

Reserve enemies may instead flee, surrender, or remain occupied if the characters sabotaged communications or created a convincing diversion.

Variant Rule Integration

Hunted

Use the campaign’s normal Hunted procedure whenever the module calls for a Hunted escalation.

Recommended escalation points include:

  • The NaviComputer’s tamper beacon transmits.

  • Witnesses clearly identify the party.

  • The characters attack Imperial personnel.

  • A probe droid records Tovan or a lightsaber.

  • The party uses captured Imperial codes after they are compromised.

  • Commander Voss survives the finale.

A Hunted complication should increase pressure without immediately ending the adventure. Good results include bounty hunters, surveillance, compromised safehouses, intercepted communications, or Imperial checkpoints.

Crueler Criticals and Wounds

The adventure assumes critical hits can create severe consequences. To prevent random early-session deaths:

  • Rustclaws retreat rather than execute fallen characters.

  • Imperial forces use stun settings until Tovan is confirmed.

  • Major enemies prioritize objectives over finishing incapacitated characters.

  • Every chapter transition offers access to medical care.

  • Environmental damage should rarely inflict critical injuries unless the danger was clearly telegraphed.

Doctor Halden Vey, Tovan Rell, and Davik’s medics can treat Wounds using the campaign’s normal rules. They do not automatically erase consequences, but they prevent injuries from making a character unplayable for several sessions.

Force Alignment

Force-sensitive characters should receive meaningful alignment pressure at the following moments:

  • Threatening Keelo after he surrenders.

  • Deciding whether to kill helpless Rustclaws.

  • Exploiting or protecting the Desert Shrine.

  • Considering whether to betray Tovan.

  • Choosing who to save during the purge.

  • Accepting Commander Voss’s bargain.

  • Using fear, rage, or cruelty against defeated enemies.

Do not treat every criminal act as a dark-side decision. Force Alignment should respond to intent, cruelty, selfishness, compassion, and sacrifice rather than simple legality.

Adventure Systems

Community Support

The party gains 1 Community Support when it meaningfully helps Bracken’s Point through a side quest or major act of public assistance.

SupportBenefit
0Residents remain suspicious and disorganized
1Locals hide the party from one routine patrol
2Advantage on one group check made inside Bracken’s Point
3The shift bells prevent one increase of the Purge Clock
4+One evacuation objective is completed by allied residents

Community Support should also influence roleplaying. At high support, residents know the characters by name and treat them as members of the community.

Search Pressure

Search Pressure represents how close the Empire is to confirming Tovan’s presence.

Begin Chapter 3 at 0, then increase it for earlier mistakes, open transmissions, surviving witnesses, probe-droid evidence, or public Force use.

PressureImperial Response
0The party is unnoticed
1Communications monitoring
2Aerial reconnaissance
3Ground search teams
4Probable Jedi activity
5Jedi confirmation and immediate purge preparation

Purge Clock

Chapter 4 uses a six-stage Purge Clock.

StageEvent
1Imperial withdrawal
2TIE attacks begin
3First orbital strike
4Infrastructure collapses
5Bracken’s Point is targeted
6Final bombardment

Advance the clock after major objectives, failed travel challenges, prolonged delays, or specified events.

Major NPCs

Tensin Black

A nervous but resourceful fixer who has promised Davik Renn a device he does not yet possess. Tensin is ambitious, evasive, and quicker to run than fight, but he is not malicious.

Davik Renn

A veteran smuggler who operates across Velsar as part of a larger syndicate. Davik values competence, discretion, and loyalty. His aging BT-9 transport, the Stargazer, is his greatest asset.

Ressik

A one-eyed Trandoshan who controls the Rustclaws through fear. Ressik wears a Wookiee-hide mantle, prizes violent spectacle, and considers himself a legendary hunter despite the dubious origins of many trophies.

Tovan Rell

A Jedi Knight who survived Order 66 and has quietly protected Velsar for years. He is compassionate, haunted, and convinced that remaining near the people he loves may condemn them.

Commander Voss

An efficient Imperial commander who views Velsar’s population as an administrative obstacle. Capturing a living Jedi could secure his career. Destroying the planet is an acceptable secondary outcome.

CHAPTER 1: A SIMPLE JOB

Chapter Goals

The characters arrive on Velsar, meet Tensin Black, recover the IN-4 navigation core from Keelo Venn, and become caught between the Rustclaws and the Empire.

The NaviComputer is divided into two parts:

  • The navigation core, held by Keelo.

  • The authentication wafer, held by Ressik.

This prevents the adventure from depending on the Rustclaws forcibly stealing the device from the party.

Scene 1: Arrival at Bracken’s Point

Use the Bracken’s Point Landing Yard map.

The transport settles onto the landing pad with a heavy metallic impact. Warning lights change from red to green, and the rear ramp begins to descend.

Bright, dusty daylight spills into the dark cargo bay.

Beyond the ramp lies Bracken’s Point: a sprawling industrial settlement of welded buildings, scaffolding, scrapyards, cranes, and smoking foundries packed into a rocky basin.

Beside the ramp, an Imperial officer waits behind a portable desk. His uniform is wrinkled, his caf is cold, and his expression suggests that your arrival has personally inconvenienced him.

Lieutenant Noll Harven processes the characters.

Questionable documents require a DC 10 Deception, Persuasion, or Technology check. Failure produces a labor assignment, minor fine, or future records review rather than arrest.

Harven directs the characters toward the Bent Spanner.

Scene 2: First Impressions

Before meeting Tensin, the party encounters a disabled cargo hauler blocking Market Row.

A DC 10 Athletics, Technology, or Persuasion check helps local workers move it.

Success earns goodwill but not yet a full Community Support point. Characters who later assist the town gain recognition more quickly.

For six players, allow two separate problems:

  • Repair the repulsor assembly.

  • Control the frustrated crowd and redirect traffic.

Scene 3: Meeting Tensin

Use the Bent Spanner Cantina map.

Tensin offers:

  • 100 credits per character in advance.

  • 500 credits total upon delivery.

  • Two nights of lodging.

  • An introduction to his buyer.

He identifies Keelo Venn as a Rustclaw slicer hiding in an abandoned compressor station.

A DC 12 Insight check reveals that Tensin is hiding the buyer’s identity and has already committed to a deadline he cannot meet.

Scene 4: The Compressor Station

Use the Abandoned Compressor Station and Eastern Scrapyard map.

Exterior Opposition

Party SizeExterior Guards
42 Rustclaw fighters
53 Rustclaw fighters
63 Rustclaw fighters; 1 reserve spotter

The party may bluff, bribe, bypass, or fight the guards.

The guards surrender or flee when half their number is incapacitated.

Keelo Venn

Keelo is frightened of Ressik and the Empire. He relinquishes the core if the characters:

  • Offer protection.

  • Defeat or bypass his guards.

  • Pay at least 100 credits.

  • Succeed on a DC 12 Intimidation check.

  • Convince him Ressik has already discovered his betrayal.

Keelo reveals that Ressik confiscated the authentication wafer.

Tamper Beacon

A DC 12 Technology check detects the core’s Imperial tamper beacon. A second DC 12 check disables it.

Failure does not destroy the device. It determines how quickly Imperial forces arrive later.

Scene 5: The Rustclaw Tail

A Rustclaw spotter follows the party if:

  • A guard escaped.

  • Keelo activated an alarm.

  • The party failed its approach check.

  • The core is carried openly.

A passive Perception of 13 or a DC 13 Perception check notices the tail.

Capturing or misleading the spotter prevents the Rustclaws from gaining favorable starting positions at the Bent Spanner.

Scene 6: Return to the Bent Spanner

Tensin scans the core and discovers the authentication wafer is missing.

He pays half the promised reward and offers the balance plus a 750-credit bonus for recovering the wafer.

Before negotiations conclude, the Rustclaws attack.

Ambush Composition

Party SizeInitial AttackersReinforcements
42 fighters1 bruiser at the end of round 3
53 fighters1 bruiser at the end of round 2
63 fighters and 1 bruiser1 fighter at the end of round 3 if the alarm remains active

The Rustclaws want the core, Keelo, and Tensin’s payment case. They do not remain to fight Imperial troops.

Imperial Arrival

  • Beacon disabled: end of round 5.

  • Beacon interrupted: end of round 4.

  • Beacon active: end of round 3.

Stormtroopers use stun weapons and attempt to detain everyone.

Escape is a group challenge:

Party SizeRequirement
43 successes before 2 failures
54 successes before 2 failures
64 successes before 3 failures

Use Athletics, Acrobatics, Stealth, Deception, Technology, Piloting, or Survival.

The party reaches Tensin’s safehouse after escaping.

Characters advance to 2nd level.

CHAPTER 2: THE RUSTCLAW REVEL

Chapter Goals

The party infiltrates Ressik’s hideout, recovers the authentication wafer and any other stolen objectives, then returns through the Imperial lockdown to meet Davik Renn.

Preparing for the Hideout

Town side quests may be completed before departure.

Useful advantages include:

  • Pavo reveals a damaged rear fence.

  • Doctor Vey’s patients provide the gate password.

  • Sella offers a concealed route and extraction plan.

  • Keelo provides the internal control-system layout.

The current Rustclaw password is Final Claim.

Hideout Roster

Use the Ressik’s Rustclaw Hideout map.

Party SizeFightersBruisersBoss
481Ressik
5102Ressik
6122Ressik

These enemies are distributed throughout the compound and never begin as a single combat group.

Suggested Distribution

Area4 PCs5 PCs6 PCs
Lookouts2 fighters2 fighters3 fighters
Vehicle yard1 fighter1 fighter2 fighters
Drinking hall3 fighters4 fighters4 fighters
Slicer station1 fighter1 fighter1 fighter
Barracks1 fighter, 1 bruiser2 fighters, 1 bruiser2 fighters, 1 bruiser
Ressik’s hallRessikRessik, 1 fighterRessik, 1 bruiser

Unused enemies are reserves, asleep, absent, or too intoxicated to respond immediately.

Alert Levels

Alert 0: Unaware

Rustclaws are drinking or sleeping. Intoxicated gang members have disadvantage on their first attack and saving throw.

Alert 1: Suspicious

One patrol investigates. Exterior doors close.

Alert 2: Mobilized

Doors lock. A gang member moves toward the slicer station.

Alert 3: Full Alarm

Reserve enemies mobilize, but no more than two ordinary enemies enter the same encounter at once.

Key Objectives

The characters may need to recover:

  • The authentication wafer.

  • The navigation core.

  • Tensin’s payment case.

  • Keelo or Tensin.

  • Pavo Nesh.

  • Rustclaw records.

Completing the mission does not require clearing the compound.

Confronting Ressik

Ressik begins with conversation unless the party has killed several Rustclaws.

He may relinquish the wafer in exchange for:

  • A dangerous future favor.

  • A valuable weapon.

  • Proof that the Empire is tracking the core.

  • Public acknowledgment of his supposed victory.

  • A personal duel.

Boss Encounter Scaling

Party SizeFinal Opposition
4Ressik alone; one fighter watches but does not enter unless the party cheats
5Ressik and 1 fighter
6Ressik and 1 bruiser; one fighter may arrive after round 3

Ressik’s allies withdraw if he is reduced below half hit points and another morale condition has been met.

Morale Conditions

  • The slicer station is controlled.

  • Keelo denounces Ressik.

  • Fraudulent trophies are exposed.

  • Escape vehicles are disabled.

  • Half the active Rustclaws are incapacitated.

  • Ressik cheats during a witnessed duel.

  • The party possesses the core and wafer.

Two morale conditions cause ordinary Rustclaws to flee or surrender.

Return Through the Southern Cut

Use the Southern Cut Imperial Checkpoint map.

The checkpoint is looking primarily for a rumored Jedi, not the NaviComputer.

The party may use Deception, Technology, Stealth, bribery, or hidden cargo compartments. The base DC is 11.

For six players, hiding the entire group without a vehicle increases the DC to 12.

Failure creates an inspection scene rather than immediate combat.

Davik Renn

Use Davik’s Reclamation Yard followed by the Hidden Stargazer Hangar map.

Davik pays the promised reward and orders his technicians to install the core and wafer.

He then asks the party to locate his missing transport, the Wayfarer.

Characters advance to 3rd level.

CHAPTER 3: THE GHOST IN THE HILLS

Chapter Goals

The party locates the Wayfarer, follows its missing pilots to Tovan Rell, and survives an Imperial reconnaissance sweep.

Locating the Wreck

Use the Crashed Transport Site map.

A search challenge requires:

Party SizeRequirement
42 successes before 2 failures
53 successes before 2 failures
63 successes before 3 failures

Use Perception, Investigation, Technology, Piloting, or Survival.

Failure damages the utility shuttle or increases Search Pressure.

Wreck Investigation

Evidence reveals:

  • The ship was attacked by military weapons.

  • Emergency medical supplies were removed.

  • The pilots were carried away alive.

  • No cargo was looted.

  • A speeder traveled east.

A DC 12 Technology check accesses the protocol droid’s recording, revealing a hooded man moving objects without touching them and carrying a lightsaber hilt.

Optional Broken Beacon

Use the Broken Beacon Escape Pod Site map.

The pod identifies Jedi Knight Tovan Rell as its occupant. Recovering the data grants advantage on the party’s first meaningful social check with Tovan.

Investigating the pod may increase Search Pressure.

Tovan’s Refuge

Use the Tovan Rell Hidden Refuge map.

Tovan has stabilized Jessa Korr and Bol Rannik.

He initially identifies himself only as Rell, a former battlefield medic. Evidence in the refuge includes:

  • Republic medical supplies.

  • Records of people he has rescued.

  • Damaged Jedi robes.

  • A concealed lightsaber.

  • The insignia of the Resolute Mercy.

Tovan reveals his identity when confronted respectfully, when Imperial forces arrive, or when the party has at least 2 Community Support.

Imperial Sweep

The sweep begins when Search Pressure reaches 3 or after the party completes its conversation with Tovan.

Encounter Composition

Party SizeImperial Force
41 investigator, 2 stormtroopers, 1 probe droid
51 investigator, 3 stormtroopers, 1 probe droid
61 investigator, 3 stormtroopers, 1 probe droid; 1 reserve trooper arriving round 4

The party’s objectives are:

  • Evacuate the injured pilots.

  • Prevent the probe droid from transmitting.

  • Preserve an escape route.

Tovan acts as a support ally rather than taking a complete independent turn. Once each round, he may heal, reposition, protect, or guide one character.

He draws his lightsaber only when someone is in immediate danger or his identity has already been exposed.

Return to Bracken’s Point

The settlement is now occupied by reinforcements, checkpoints, and probe droids.

Davik’s technicians reveal Contingency Cinderglass, an authorization permitting orbital sterilization if Jedi activity is confirmed.

A Star Destroyer is entering the system.

Characters advance to 4th level.

CHAPTER 4: FIRE FROM THE SKY

Chapter Goals

The party prepares the evacuation, rescues as many people as possible, confronts Commander Voss, launches the Stargazer, and escapes the interdiction field.

Preparation Time

Search PressurePreparation Scenes
0–22
31
41 hurried scene with disadvantage
5None

Available preparations include:

  • Ready the Stargazer.

  • Warn the neighborhoods.

  • Establish an escape route.

  • Secure medical supplies.

  • Steal Imperial codes.

  • Contact outer settlements.

For six players, the party may split into two groups during one preparation scene. Both groups make separate checks, but any failure causes one complication or advances Imperial awareness.

Imperial Withdrawal

The Empire removes personnel, burns records, and dismantles checkpoints.

The Star Destroyer descends into low orbit.

The Purge Clock begins at 1.

Evacuation Objectives

The party should be able to pursue more objectives with additional players, but time remains limited.

Available Objectives

  1. Evacuate the Workers’ Blocks.

  2. Rescue prisoners.

  3. Recover the final navigation key.

  4. Save Doctor Vey’s clinic.

  5. Preserve the Stargazer.

  6. Save Tovan Rell.

Recommended Objective Expectations

Party SizeStrong OutcomeBest Outcome
43 completed4 completed
53 completed5 completed
64 completed5–6 completed

Completing additional objectives should be possible because larger parties can divide their attention, not because each objective is easier.

Splitting the Party

During the purge, five- or six-character parties may form subgroups.

Each subgroup must contain at least two characters. Resolve one scene for each subgroup before advancing the Purge Clock.

If one subgroup fails a travel challenge, the clock advances after all current subgroup scenes conclude.

Tovan, Davik, and other allies may accompany a subgroup but do not replace player characters.

Prisoner Transfer

Use the Prisoner Transfer Ambush Site map.

Party SizeConvoy Guards
41 investigator, 2 stormtroopers, 1 security droid
51 investigator, 3 stormtroopers, 1 security droid
61 investigator, 3 stormtroopers, 1 security droid; 1 reserve trooper

The convoy can be redirected, disabled, infiltrated, or ambushed.

Released prisoners seek cover rather than joining the initiative order.

Administration Square

Use the Administration Square and Detention Center map if prisoners reach the garrison or the party must recover codes and the navigation key.

The garrison should contain no more than:

Party SizeActive Opposition
42 troopers and 1 investigator
53 troopers and 1 investigator
63 troopers, 1 investigator, and 1 security droid in a separate section

Additional personnel are evacuating, occupied, or already gone.

Workers’ Blocks and Market Row

Use the Workers’ Blocks Evacuation and Market Row During the Purge maps.

These scenes focus on travel, civilians, collapsing structures, and TIE strikes rather than conventional stand-up combat.

A travel challenge normally requires:

Party SizeRequirement
43 successes before 2 failures
54 successes before 2 failures
64 successes before 3 failures

Characters cannot repeat the same skill unless circumstances change.

Final Hangar Encounter

Use the Hidden Stargazer Hangar map.

Standard Opposition

Party SizeStarting EnemiesReinforcements
4Voss, 1 stormtrooper, 1 security droid1 trooper at end of round 3
5Voss, 2 stormtroopers, 1 security droidNone unless alarm remains active
6Voss, 2 stormtroopers, 1 security droid1 trooper at end of round 3 and another at round 5 only if the party has several combat allies

Voss prioritizes the NaviComputer, Tovan, and the ship. He does not attack unconscious characters unless no other objective remains.

Hangar Objectives

Select unresolved objectives according to preparation and surviving allies.

Party SizeObjectives Required During Combat
43
54
65, but two may be attempted simultaneously

Possible objectives:

  • Release docking clamps.

  • Complete NaviComputer installation.

  • Open the launch tunnel.

  • Disconnect fuel lines.

  • Remove the Imperial tracker.

  • Protect boarding civilians.

  • Restore auxiliary power.

Allies resolve one objective each at the GM’s discretion, based on who survived and what preparations were completed.

Environmental Events

At initiative count 20:

  1. Hangar tremor.

  2. Power failure.

  3. Orbital debris strike.

  4. Catwalk collapse.

  5. Launch tunnel damage.

  6. Final bombardment.

Environmental events should change the battlefield rather than simply deal unavoidable damage.

Launch Challenge

The Stargazer requires the following number of successes before three failures:

Party SizeRequired Successes
44
55
66

Each character may attempt one meaningful task before another character repeats the same skill.

Automatic successes may come from:

  • Preparing the ship.

  • Rescuing Bol or Jessa.

  • Recovering Imperial codes.

  • Keelo completing the installation.

  • Completing four or more evacuation objectives.

Failure still allows escape but adds serious complications.

Side Quests

Town Quests

The Missing Mechanic

Party SizeOpposition
42 fighters
53 fighters
63 fighters and 1 reserve fighter

Pavo’s rescue provides vehicle sabotage during Chapter 2 and repair support during Chapter 4.

Trouble at the Cantina

Primarily social. If violence occurs, use one stormtrooper per two characters, but have civilians, exits, and conflicting objectives prevent a simple firefight.

The Street Doc’s Dilemma

An Imperial investigator arrives with:

  • Four PCs: 1 trooper.

  • Five PCs: 2 troopers.

  • Six PCs: 2 troopers and a probe droid.

The encounter is about concealment and moral choices rather than combat.

Wilderness Quests

The Vanishing Caravan

Party SizeRaiders
43 fighters
54 fighters
64 fighters and 1 bruiser arriving after combat begins

The Desert Shrine

The shrine should test exploration and Force-sensitive choices. Use scavengers or wildlife in separated groups.

  • Four PCs: 3 ordinary enemies.

  • Five PCs: 4 ordinary enemies.

  • Six PCs: 4 ordinary enemies and 1 stronger creature.

The Broken Beacon

Primarily exploration. If wildlife is present, use environmental positioning and territorial behavior rather than enemies that fight to the death.

Imperial Quests

Checkpoint Trouble

Combat is intentionally dangerous.

Party SizeCheckpoint Personnel
41 officer and 3 troopers
51 officer and 4 troopers
61 officer, 4 troopers, and 1 probe droid

Bypassing, bribing, slicing, or deceiving the checkpoint should remain preferable.

Prisoner Transfer

Use the Chapter 4 convoy scaling, but remove one trooper if the quest occurs before the characters reach 4th level.

Medical and Rest Opportunities

Because the campaign uses Wounds and Crueler Criticals, place reliable recovery opportunities between major chapters.

After Chapter 1

Tensin’s safehouse contains basic medical supplies. Doctor Vey can be introduced immediately if a character suffered a Wound.

After Chapter 2

Davik’s hangar contains a functional medbay and several experienced crew medics.

After Chapter 3

Tovan or Doctor Vey can stabilize serious injuries before the purge begins.

During Chapter 4

Saving Doctor Vey’s clinic allows one protected short rest without advancing the Purge Clock.

The party should never be guaranteed full recovery during the purge.

Adventure Outcomes

Zero to One Evacuation Objective

Only scattered individuals escape. Bracken’s Point is effectively erased.

Two Objectives

A fragmented group of survivors reaches the wilderness or evacuation craft.

Three Objectives

A significant civilian population survives, and Davik’s organization remains partially functional.

Four Objectives

Most named allies and organized neighborhoods escape.

Five or More Objectives

The Empire destroys Bracken’s Point but fails to erase its people or their testimony.

Continuing the Campaign

The party may leave Velsar with:

  • The BT-9 Stargazer.

  • Velsar refugees.

  • Tovan Rell.

  • Commander Voss as an enemy or prisoner.

  • Evidence of Contingency Cinderglass.

  • An incomplete or compromised Imperial NaviComputer.

  • Debts owed to Davik’s larger syndicate.

Likely follow-up adventures include finding sanctuary, repairing the Stargazer, evading Voss, rescuing Tovan, exposing the purge, or investigating the NaviComputer’s classified destination.

Emergency Three-Player Adjustment

The adventure is intended for at least four characters. When only three players attend:

  • Use the four-player enemy count minus one ordinary enemy.

  • Do not remove the primary boss.

  • Allow one allied NPC to perform one support effect each round.

  • Reduce multi-success challenges by one required success.

  • Give the party an additional medpac or temporary safe route.

  • Never add reinforcements unless the party raises a full alarm.

This allows an occasional absence without rewriting the session while preserving the campaign’s dangerous tone.
