Chapter 4: Fire from the Sky

The characters begin this chapter at 4th level. Commander Voss has confirmed that a Jedi survivor is operating on Velsar, and the approaching Star Destroyer carries authorization to enact Contingency Cinderglass.

The Empire first arrests suspected collaborators, seizes the settlement’s communications, and withdraws its personnel. Once Imperial forces have cleared the target zone, orbital bombardment begins.

The characters cannot defeat the Star Destroyer or save every inhabitant of Velsar. Their objectives are to preserve as much of Bracken’s Point as possible, reach the Stargazer, and escape through the Imperial interdiction perimeter.

The decisions made throughout the adventure determine who survives, how difficult the evacuation becomes, and whether the characters leave Velsar as fugitives, smugglers, or the beginnings of a resistance movement.

Chapter Overview

The characters:

  1. Learn how much time remains before the Imperial withdrawal.

  2. Prepare allies, equipment, and evacuation routes.

  3. Respond to mass arrests and raids in Bracken’s Point.

  4. Recognize that the Imperial evacuation signals an imminent bombardment.

  5. Choose which people and objectives they will attempt to save.

  6. Navigate Bracken’s Point while TIE fighters and orbital fire destroy the settlement.

  7. Confront Commander Voss at Davik’s hidden hangar.

  8. Launch aboard the Stargazer.

  9. Use the stolen NaviComputer to cross the interdiction field.

  10. Determine who and what survives the destruction of Velsar.

1. Beginning the Chapter

The chapter begins inside Davik Renn’s hidden hangar shortly after the characters discover Contingency Cinderglass.

Davik’s technicians are completing the integration of the Imperial NaviComputer. The Stargazer can fly, but several systems remain disconnected while the installation is finalized.

Outside the hangar, Commander Voss’s forces begin coordinated arrests across Bracken’s Point.

Opening Boxed Text

The hidden hangar trembles beneath the distant passage of heavy transports.

Mechanics move rapidly beneath the Stargazer, reconnecting access panels and dragging fuel lines away from the ship. At the navigation station, Imperial fleet movements spread across the display in tightening patterns.

Red markers surround Velsar.

Davik studies the data in silence.

“The interdiction ships are already moving into position.”

Another transmission appears. Arrest lists. Seizure orders. Neighborhood searches.

Then the public communication network cuts to static.

Somewhere above, the shift bells begin ringing again.

This time, they do not stop.

2. Determine the Starting Situation

Several results from Chapter 3 affect the beginning of the finale.

Search Pressure

The party’s final Search Pressure determines how much time it has to prepare.

Search PressurePreparation Time
0–2Two preparation scenes
3One preparation scene
4One hurried preparation scene made with disadvantage
5No preparation scenes; Voss immediately contacts the party

A preparation scene represents approximately one hour of coordinated activity.

The characters may split up, but each preparation scene should focus on one major objective.

Tovan’s Status

Tovan Is with the Party

Tovan assists with planning but argues that he should leave Bracken’s Point and draw Imperial forces away.

He can accompany one preparation scene without drawing attention if concealed.

Tovan Is Hidden in Bracken’s Point

Tovan is sheltering at Doctor Vey’s clinic, a neighborhood safehouse, or another location chosen earlier.

An Imperial investigation team is moving toward his location.

Tovan Remains in the Wilderness

Tovan has begun warning outer settlements.

He can reach Bracken’s Point later, but doing so increases the risk of interception.

Tovan Was Captured

He is being transported to the Imperial garrison for identification before transfer to the Star Destroyer.

The characters may attempt to rescue him during the mass arrests or allow his capture to distract Voss.

Tovan Is Missing

Davik receives an uncertain report of a lone figure moving toward the Southern Cut. Tovan’s fate remains unresolved until later in the chapter.

Davik’s Pilots

If Jessa Korr and Bol Rannik were rescued, they assist with preparing the Stargazer.

Each surviving pilot provides one benefit:

Jessa Korr

Jessa can pilot the Stargazer during launch, allowing a player character to operate weapons, engineering, or navigation.

Bol Rannik

Bol completes emergency repairs. The party gains one automatic success during the final launch sequence.

If both pilots remain captured, they are included among the prisoners being transferred from Bracken’s Point.

3. Preparation Scenes

Each preparation scene provides a benefit during the evacuation.

The characters should know they cannot complete every option. Their limited time forces them to decide what matters most.

Prepare the Stargazer

The characters assist Davik’s crew with repairs and the NaviComputer installation.

The group must achieve three successes before two failures.

Possible checks include:

  • DC 12 Intelligence (Technology): Integrate the Imperial navigation core.

  • DC 11 Strength (Athletics): Move heavy equipment or release jammed components.

  • DC 12 Piloting: Calibrate flight controls.

  • DC 12 Intelligence (Investigation): Trace a damaged circuit.

  • DC 11 Dexterity check with appropriate tools: Repair exposed connections.

Success

The Stargazer is ready to launch when the party reaches the hangar.

The party gains two automatic successes during the launch sequence.

Failure

The ship remains flyable, but one major system fails during launch. The GM chooses shields, weapons, sensors, or maneuvering thrusters.

The party must repair or compensate for that system later.

Warn the Neighborhoods

The characters coordinate with workers, local leaders, and neighborhood watches.

This can be accomplished through the shift bells, runners, short-range comlinks, or Davik’s contacts.

Use a DC 12 group Charisma or Intelligence check. Characters may use Persuasion, Deception, Technology, or an appropriate background skill.

Success

Residents begin moving toward old mines, ore tunnels, and protected shelters before the bombardment.

Complete the Evacuate the Neighborhoods objective automatically.

Failure

The warning spreads unevenly. Civilians begin evacuating only after the first orbital strike.

The objective remains available during the Purge Clock.

Establish an Escape Route

The characters examine the city map and choose a route from central Bracken’s Point to Davik’s hangar.

Possible routes include:

  • Market Row and the Freight Quarter

  • The rooftops of the Workers’ Blocks

  • The Southern Cut

  • Sella Vorn’s smuggling tunnels

  • The old industrial service roads

  • The abandoned ore conduits

The party must succeed on a DC 12 Survival, Investigation, or Technology check.

Success

The chosen route remains accessible until Purge Clock 5.

The party has advantage on its first travel challenge during the bombardment.

Failure

The route appears usable but becomes blocked at Purge Clock 3.

The party must improvise another way through the settlement.

Secure Medical Supplies

The characters help Doctor Vey relocate patients and prepare emergency supplies.

This requires a DC 11 Medicine, Technology, or Persuasion check.

Success

The party receives:

  • Two medpacs

  • One trauma kit

  • One emergency stimulant

  • Access to a protected treatment shelter

During the final chapter, each character can regain 5 hit points once after completing an evacuation objective.

Failure

The supplies are gathered, but Doctor Vey refuses to abandon several patients. The clinic becomes an optional evacuation objective.

Steal Imperial Codes

The characters infiltrate Administration Square, capture a courier, or intercept encrypted transmissions.

This preparation scene may be run as a brief skill challenge requiring two successes before two failures.

Appropriate checks include:

  • DC 13 Stealth

  • DC 12 Deception

  • DC 12 Technology

  • DC 13 Sleight of Hand

  • DC 12 Insight

Success

The characters acquire current Imperial authorization codes.

Once during the chapter, they may:

  • Pass an Imperial checkpoint automatically.

  • Delay a patrol for 1 minute.

  • Open a secured Imperial door.

  • Transmit a false evacuation order.

  • Cancel one increase of the Purge Clock caused by Imperial opposition.

Failure

The party acquires outdated codes. They work once, but the Empire recognizes them as compromised immediately afterward.

Commander Voss learns the party is active in Bracken’s Point.

Contact Outer Settlements

The characters send warnings to remote miners, farms, salvage camps, and small communities outside the primary bombardment zone.

This requires a DC 12 Technology or Persuasion check.

Success

Many outer settlements begin evacuating into the wilderness.

The number of surviving Velsar civilians significantly increases.

If Tovan remained outside Bracken’s Point, he receives the warning and begins guiding survivors.

Failure

The Empire traces the transmission.

The warning still reaches some settlements, but Voss learns which communications network the party is using.

4. Community Support

Community Support earned during earlier chapters becomes critical now.

0 Support: Fractured Settlement

Residents panic independently. Streets clog with vehicles, rumors, and frightened crowds.

The party has disadvantage on its first group travel check during the purge.

1 Support: Familiar Faces

Local residents recognize the party and provide temporary shelter.

The characters can hide from one patrol without making a check.

2 Support: Quiet Assistance

Workers open private passages and move obstacles.

The party gains advantage on one group check of its choice during the chapter.

3 Support: The Shift Bells

The neighborhoods use coordinated bell patterns to communicate through the Imperial jamming.

Cancel one increase of the Purge Clock.

4 or More Support: Velsar Stands Together

Repair crews, neighborhood watches, haulers, and smugglers organize a coordinated evacuation.

Choose one objective other than confronting Voss. That objective is completed without the characters needing to pursue it personally.

5. The Mass Arrests

Before withdrawing, the Empire attempts to detain anyone connected to Tovan, Davik, the Rustclaws, or the stolen NaviComputer.

The characters receive reports of raids throughout Bracken’s Point.

Arrests Boxed Text

The first clear transmission comes from a neighborhood emergency channel.

“Imperials in the Workers’ Blocks. They are taking everyone from Building Twelve.”

Another voice interrupts.

“Transports moving toward Administration Square. Dozens of prisoners.”

Blaster fire sounds through the receiver.

Then a calm Imperial announcement replaces every channel.

“Remain inside your assigned residence. Interference with authorized security operations will be punished.”

Davik shuts off the speaker.

“They are collecting witnesses before they burn the evidence.”

The characters may intervene immediately or remain focused on preparation.

Intervening begins one of the following encounters.

6. Optional Encounter: The Prisoner Transfer

Use the Prisoner Transfer Ambush Site battlemap.

The convoy carries people connected to the party. Choose prisoners based on previous outcomes:

  • Tovan Rell

  • Jessa Korr or Bol Rannik

  • Tensin Black

  • Keelo Venn

  • Pavo Nesh

  • Sella Vorn

  • Doctor Vey

  • Captured Rustclaws

  • Neighborhood leaders

Convoy Composition

Use:

  • 2 Imperial prisoner transports

  • 2 stormtroopers

  • 1 Imperial investigator

  • 1 security droid

Two additional stormtroopers arrive after three rounds if an alarm is transmitted.

The convoy is dangerous for four 4th-level characters but manageable if the party uses terrain, sabotage, or deception.

Approaching the Convoy

The party may:

  • Ambush the vehicles at the canyon crossroads.

  • Block the road with industrial machinery.

  • Pose as Imperial personnel.

  • Slice the convoy’s route instructions.

  • Use the stolen codes to redirect the transports.

  • Follow the convoy to Administration Square.

  • Allow Tovan to escape using the Force from inside.

Sabotaging the Road

A character may use explosives, machinery, or terrain with a DC 12 Technology, Athletics, or Survival check.

On a success, one transport stops in a vulnerable position.

On a failure, the convoy detects the obstacle and deploys its security droid before reaching it.

Freeing the Prisoners

Each transport has AC 15 and a secured rear door.

The door can be opened with:

  • A captured Imperial key cylinder

  • DC 13 Technology

  • 20 damage against AC 15

  • Imperial access codes

  • A prisoner opening it from within

Released prisoners do not normally join combat. They seek cover and follow the characters’ directions.

Tovan Inside the Convoy

If Tovan is imprisoned, he refrains from using his powers until civilians are endangered.

Once the rear door opens, he protects the prisoners and creates an escape route rather than attacking the convoy guards.

Convoy Outcome

Complete Success

All prisoners are rescued, and the Empire cannot identify where they went.

Complete the Rescue the Prisoners objective.

Partial Success

The party rescues one transport’s occupants while the other continues toward the garrison.

The remaining prisoners can be rescued later, but doing so costs time.

Failure

The convoy reaches Administration Square.

The prisoners are still alive and may be freed during the withdrawal, but Voss gains leverage over the party.

7. The Imperial Withdrawal

The withdrawal begins after the characters complete their preparation scenes or prisoner-transfer encounter.

Withdrawal Boxed Text

The change begins quietly.

Stormtroopers abandon the outer checkpoints. Officers carry sealed cases from Administration Square. Communications equipment is dismantled, vehicles loaded, and records burned in metal bins.

Imperial transports rise from the Landing Yard in disciplined formations.

Civilians emerge from doorways and watch them leave.

For the first time in days, no white-armored patrols occupy the streets.

Then a triangular shadow appears above the clouds.

It grows until it covers half the sky.

The Star Destroyer descends into low orbit over Bracken’s Point.

Tovan looks upward.

“They are clearing the target.”

The residents initially believe the occupation is ending.

The characters have only minutes to convince people otherwise.

8. The Purge Clock

The remainder of the chapter uses a six-stage Purge Clock.

Begin at Purge Clock 1 when the Star Destroyer enters low orbit.

Increase the clock:

  • After each major evacuation objective

  • When the party fails a travel challenge

  • When the party takes a short rest outside a protected shelter

  • When the characters spend excessive time debating or searching

  • When an encounter triggers Imperial reinforcements

  • When specified by an event

Community Support and successful preparation can prevent some increases.

Purge Clock 1: Imperial Withdrawal

Imperial forces evacuate the primary target zones.

  • Communications are jammed.

  • Major checkpoints are abandoned.

  • Civilians gather in streets.

  • The Landing Yard begins closing.

  • Voss’s remaining security units move toward Davik’s hangar.

The characters may move normally.

Purge Clock 2: TIE Strikes

TIE fighters attack roads, power stations, communications towers, and civilian transports.

Whenever the party crosses an exposed outdoor area, one character must make a DC 12 Wisdom (Perception) or Piloting check.

On a failure, the group must take cover or suffer 7 (2d6) energy damage each, halved with a successful DC 12 Dexterity saving throw.

Purge Clock 3: First Orbital Salvo

A distant settlement is destroyed.

A line of green light descends beyond the western ridges.

For half a second, nothing happens.

Then the horizon becomes white.

The shockwave reaches Bracken’s Point moments later. Windows burst inward. Walkways twist from their supports, and the ground bucks beneath your feet.

Far beyond the settlement wall, a column of fire rises into the sky.

Everyone understands that Bracken’s Point is next.

All civilian movement becomes difficult. Group travel checks increase by 1 DC unless the party has at least 3 Community Support.

Purge Clock 4: Infrastructure Collapse

Power fails across most of the settlement.

  • Cargo lifts stop.

  • Fires spread through the Foundry Ward.

  • Market Row becomes blocked by wreckage.

  • The Landing Yard suffers repeated TIE strikes.

  • Several old tunnels collapse.

All Technology checks involving city systems are made with disadvantage unless a portable power source is available.

Purge Clock 5: Bracken’s Point Targeted

Orbital fire begins striking the edge of the industrial basin.

At the beginning of each major scene, choose or roll one environmental event:

  1. A nearby building collapses.

  2. A repulsor vehicle crashes into the street.

  3. A shockwave knocks creatures prone.

  4. A fire blocks the direct route.

  5. Panicked civilians flood the area.

  6. Imperial debris falls from above.

Characters outside hard cover when a strike lands must make a DC 13 Dexterity saving throw, taking 10 (3d6) kinetic or fire damage on a failure or half as much on a success.

Purge Clock 6: Final Bombardment

Bracken’s Point is consumed.

Once the clock reaches 6, the characters have one final scene to launch the Stargazer or leave the basin by another means.

Any unresolved evacuation objectives are lost unless an ally can complete them.

9. Evacuation Objectives

The characters cannot personally complete every objective.

They should choose what to prioritize while allies address the rest.

Completing three objectives produces a broadly successful evacuation. Completing four or more produces the best possible ending.

Objective 1: Evacuate the Neighborhoods

Hundreds of civilians shelter inside the Workers’ Blocks, believing the buildings will protect them.

The party must convince them to move into old excavation tunnels or board available transports.

Reaching the Blocks

The characters must complete a group travel check requiring three successes before two failures.

Appropriate skills include:

  • Athletics

  • Acrobatics

  • Survival

  • Technology

  • Persuasion

  • Perception

The base DC is 12.

Organizing the Evacuation

Once there, a character must make a DC 13 Persuasion or Intimidation check.

The check is made with advantage if:

  • The party earned at least 2 Community Support.

  • Mira or Pavo Nesh is present.

  • The shift bells remain operational.

  • The characters witnessed the destruction of another settlement.

  • Tovan openly helps the evacuation.

Success

Residents move through the old mining tunnels before the bombardment reaches the district.

Failure

The civilians hesitate until an orbital strike hits nearby. They begin evacuating, but the Purge Clock increases by 1.

Objective 2: Rescue the Prisoners

This objective is completed if the party successfully intercepted the prisoner convoy.

If not, prisoners are held at Administration Square while Imperial personnel prepare to evacuate.

Use:

  • 2 stormtroopers

  • 1 Imperial investigator

  • Remaining checkpoint personnel

  • Environmental chaos

The characters may infiltrate the detention area using abandoned Imperial uniforms or the stolen codes.

Freeing the prisoners requires a DC 13 Technology check or access key.

Success

The prisoners escape through the Freight Quarter or old service roads.

Failure

The party frees some prisoners, but the Imperial transport departs with the rest. Tovan may surrender himself to stop the departure if he is present.

Objective 3: Recover the Final Navigation Key

The NaviComputer installation requires a final decryption key held in a portable Imperial slicer terminal.

The location of the key depends on previous events.

Tensin Has the Key

Tensin stole the key during the confusion and is attempting to reach Davik’s hangar.

If the party treated him well, he contacts them and arranges a meeting.

If the party repeatedly threatened or abandoned him, he considers selling it to Voss in exchange for passage offworld.

The Empire Has the Key

The key is stored at Administration Square or carried by the Imperial investigator in the prisoner convoy.

Keelo Has the Key

Keelo can complete the installation if brought safely to the Stargazer.

Recovering the Key

A character can obtain it through:

  • Negotiation

  • Theft

  • Combat

  • DC 13 Technology to reconstruct it from partial records

  • Imperial access codes

Without the key, the Stargazer can still attempt to escape, but the hyperspace route becomes substantially more dangerous.

Objective 4: Save Doctor Vey’s Clinic

Doctor Vey refuses to leave without his wounded patients.

The clinic contains:

  • Doctor Vey

  • Four immobile patients

  • Two frightened assistants

  • Medical supplies

  • A damaged repulsor stretcher

The party must obtain transport or move the patients into a reinforced industrial tunnel.

Possible solutions include:

  • Repairing the stretcher with DC 11 Technology

  • Finding a cargo hauler

  • Convincing workers to help

  • Using Tovan’s abilities

  • Carrying patients individually

  • Calling in an ally

Success

Doctor Vey, his patients, and the clinic supplies survive.

The party may immediately complete a short rest without advancing the Purge Clock once during the chapter.

Failure

Vey orders the party to leave while he remains behind. He can still survive if the characters previously earned his loyalty and secured a shelter.

Objective 5: Preserve the Stargazer

The Empire has discovered Davik’s reclamation yard.

Voss dispatches troops to seal the underground hangar and activate magnetic docking clamps.

Before the final confrontation, the characters must prevent one or more of the following:

  • The hangar entrance being sealed

  • Fuel lines being destroyed

  • The docking clamps engaging

  • The launch tunnel collapsing

  • Imperial tracking devices being installed

Davik’s crew can handle one problem without assistance.

Each surviving pilot handles one additional problem.

The characters must resolve any remaining problems during the final hangar encounter.

Objective 6: Save Tovan Rell

Tovan believes he is the cause of the purge and intends to lead the Empire away from civilians.

His plan may involve:

  • Surrendering to Voss

  • Attacking Imperial transports

  • Drawing TIE fighters into the hills

  • Remaining behind while the Stargazer launches

  • Creating a visible diversion in Bracken’s Point

Convincing Tovan to Escape

A character may make a DC 14 Charisma (Persuasion) check.

The check is made with advantage if:

  • The party protected the Desert Shrine.

  • The party rescued civilians before seeking Tovan.

  • At least three evacuation objectives are complete.

  • A Force-sensitive character appeals to him.

  • The party argues that helping future survivors is more important than dying on Velsar.

Success

Tovan agrees to board the Stargazer or assist the evacuation before leaving.

Failure

Tovan refuses to flee unless the characters physically prevent him or demonstrate that his surrender will accomplish nothing.

10. Commander Voss’s Offer

Voss contacts the party after the Purge Clock reaches 3 or after the characters complete two objectives.

Voss’s Transmission

Every functioning comlink in the area activates at once.

Commander Voss appears through heavy static, his gray uniform immaculate despite the chaos behind him.

“You have demonstrated unusual persistence.”

His gaze settles directly on the recorder.

“Surrender Jedi fugitive Tovan Rell and the stolen Imperial navigation core. One vessel will be permitted to leave Velsar before sterilization is complete.”

The image flickers.

“Refuse, and the people assisting you will be designated active insurgents.”

Voss pauses.

“This offer expires when the bombardment reaches Bracken’s Point.”

Voss intends to allow one vessel to launch if both Tovan and the core are surrendered.

He also intends to track, intercept, and arrest the vessel after it clears the atmosphere.

A character who succeeds on a DC 13 Wisdom (Insight) check realizes Voss is withholding part of his plan.

Tovan believes Voss might delay the bombardment long enough for some civilians to escape.

Davik insists that Voss cannot be trusted.

Accepting the Offer

If the party accepts, Voss orders the bombardment paused briefly.

The party gains time to complete one evacuation objective without advancing the Purge Clock.

Voss demands the exchange occur at Davik’s hangar.

During the meeting, the characters may:

  • Complete the surrender

  • Betray Voss

  • Plant a tracker or explosive

  • Stage Tovan’s escape

  • Hand over a false NaviComputer

  • Use the pause to launch

Voss expects deception and brings additional security.

11. Traveling Through the Bombardment

Whenever the party moves between districts after Purge Clock 2, use a travel challenge.

The characters require three successes before two failures.

Suitable checks include:

  • Athletics: Move wreckage or climb collapsed structures.

  • Acrobatics: Cross broken walkways.

  • Perception: Identify incoming attacks.

  • Piloting: Drive through damaged roads.

  • Survival: Find stable routes.

  • Technology: Operate damaged city machinery.

  • Persuasion: Move panicked crowds.

  • Stealth: Avoid Imperial remnants.

The base DC is 12, increasing to 13 at Purge Clock 5.

Success

The party reaches its destination without advancing the clock.

One Failure

Each character takes 3 (1d6) damage, or the group loses a useful piece of equipment.

Two Failures

The party reaches its destination, but the Purge Clock increases by 1.

12. Return to Davik’s Hangar

Use the Davik Renn’s Hidden Stargazer Hangar battlemap.

By the time the party arrives, Imperial forces have breached the reclamation yard.

Hangar Boxed Text

Smoke fills the excavation chamber.

The Stargazer stands at the center of the hangar surrounded by abandoned tools, severed fuel lines, and sparking machinery. Davik’s crew fires from behind cargo crates while white-armored troops move along the upper platforms.

A magnetic clamp has locked around the ship’s forward landing strut.

At the far end of the chamber, Commander Voss steps through the smoke with a security droid at his side.

His voice carries across the hangar.

“You were given an opportunity to survive.”

13. Final Encounter

A standard final encounter for four 4th-level characters includes:

  • Commander Voss

  • 2 stormtroopers

  • 1 Imperial security droid

One additional stormtrooper enters at the end of round 3 if the party has completed fewer than three evacuation objectives.

Another may arrive at the end of round 5 if Voss transmitted a reinforcement request.

Do not begin with Voss, four stormtroopers, and the droid all attacking simultaneously unless the party has several powerful allies present.

Allied Participation

Allies should perform tasks rather than add full combat turns.

Davik Renn

Davik directs his crew and provides covering fire.

Once during the encounter, he can allow one character to move up to half its speed or make one weapon attack as a reaction.

Tovan Rell

Tovan protects civilians and prevents structural collapse.

Once per round, he provides one of his support effects. He confronts Voss directly only if the characters are overwhelmed.

Jessa Korr

Jessa begins the launch sequence.

Bol Rannik

Bol attempts to release the docking clamps.

Keelo Venn

Keelo installs the final navigation key or disables Imperial systems.

Pavo Nesh

Pavo repairs the launch controls or opens the maintenance exit.

Sella Vorn

Sella holds off reinforcements from an upper platform.

Doctor Vey

Vey stabilizes injured characters and crew members behind cover.

14. Hangar Objectives

The characters must complete several objectives while fighting Voss.

Determine which remain unresolved based on preparation and surviving allies.

A standard encounter should require the party to complete three objectives.

Release the Docking Clamp

A character adjacent to the clamp console can use an action and make a DC 13 Technology check.

Alternatively, the clamp has AC 16, 25 hit points, and immunity to psychic damage.

On a failed Technology check, the clamp releases partially. A second attempt is made with advantage.

Complete the NaviComputer Installation

A character at the navigation terminal must achieve two successful DC 12 Technology checks.

Keelo automatically provides one success if present.

Without the final key, the DC becomes 15.

Open the Launch Tunnel

Imperial forces have sealed the outer doors.

A character can:

  • Use stolen codes

  • Reach the upper control room

  • Make a DC 13 Technology check

  • Destroy the door controls

  • Activate the emergency release

Failure causes the doors to open slowly. The ship cannot launch until the end of the following round.

Disconnect the Fuel Lines

Two fuel lines remain attached to the ship.

Each can be disconnected with an action.

Launching while a line remains attached causes an explosion dealing 10 (3d6) fire damage to all creatures within 15 feet of the ship and damages the Stargazer.

Remove the Imperial Tracker

Voss’s security droid has attached a tracking beacon beneath the aft hull.

A character must reach the maintenance trench and succeed on a DC 12 Investigation or Technology check.

If the tracker is not removed, Imperial forces can pursue the Stargazer after it escapes Velsar.

15. Environmental Events

At initiative count 20, one environmental event occurs each round.

Do not repeat an event unless necessary.

Round 1: Hangar Tremor

Each creature on an elevated platform must succeed on a DC 11 Dexterity saving throw or fall prone.

Round 2: Power Failure

The main lights shut down.

Areas beyond emergency lights become heavily obscured until auxiliary power is restored with a DC 11 Technology check.

Round 3: Incoming Strike

A nearby orbital impact showers the hangar with debris.

Each creature not behind substantial cover must make a DC 12 Dexterity saving throw, taking 5 (1d10) kinetic damage on a failure.

Round 4: Structural Collapse

One catwalk or elevated platform collapses.

Creatures standing on it must succeed on a DC 12 Dexterity saving throw or fall 15 feet.

Round 5: Launch Tunnel Damage

The launch tunnel begins collapsing.

The party has three rounds to launch before the primary route becomes impassable.

Round 6: Final Salvo

The Purge Clock immediately advances to 6.

The characters must board the Stargazer or escape through the maintenance tunnels before the end of the following round.

16. Voss’s Tactics

Voss remains behind cover and uses the security droid to protect him.

His priorities are:

  1. Capture Tovan.

  2. Secure the NaviComputer.

  3. Prevent the Stargazer from launching.

  4. Escape if the hangar becomes unsalvageable.

Voss does not fight to the death.

When reduced below half hit points, he moves toward an Imperial shuttle, upper access tunnel, or reinforced control room.

If escape becomes impossible, he attempts to negotiate.

“Killing me will not stop the bombardment. It will only ensure that no one remains to order it delayed.”

Voss can delay one strike if the characters spare him, but he cannot cancel Contingency Cinderglass without authorization from the Star Destroyer.

17. Defeating Voss

The characters may resolve the confrontation in several ways.

Voss Is Killed

Imperial forces lose tactical coordination, but the bombardment continues.

Evidence recovered from his body includes:

  • His command cylinder

  • Contingency Cinderglass orders

  • Prisoner records

  • Imperial tracking frequencies

  • A list of suspected Jedi sympathizers

Voss Is Captured

Voss can be used to transmit false orders or delay pursuit.

A successful DC 13 Intimidation, Deception, or Technology check forces or imitates an order recalling nearby TIE fighters.

Voss becomes a dangerous prisoner and potential source of information.

Voss Escapes

Voss reaches an Imperial transport or secure passage.

He becomes a recurring antagonist and personally leads the pursuit of the Stargazer.

Voss Surrenders

Voss surrenders only if wounded, isolated, and unable to escape.

He remains calm and attempts to manipulate the party into prioritizing him over civilians.

18. Launching the Stargazer

Once the required hangar objectives are complete, the characters must board the ship.

The Stargazer has limited space. Cargo bays, maintenance passages, and crew compartments can hold more passengers than the vessel was designed to carry, but conditions are cramped and dangerous.

Davik refuses to leave while surviving crew members remain in the hangar unless the party convinces him that staying will kill everyone aboard.

Launch Boxed Text

The Stargazer’s engines ignite with a roar that shakes dust from the cavern roof.

Emergency lights flash along the open boarding ramp as civilians, smugglers, and wounded crew members crowd into the ship.

Davik takes the pilot’s seat and pulls the control yoke toward him.

“Clamps?”

A warning light turns green.

“Tunnel?”

The outer doors begin to separate.

Behind the ship, the hangar wall fractures beneath another impact.

Davik looks toward the controls.

“Then let us see whether this old thing remembers how to run.”

19. Launch Challenge

The launch requires four successes before three failures.

One character may attempt each check per round. A character cannot use the same skill twice unless circumstances change.

Possible checks include:

  • DC 13 Piloting: Navigate the collapsing launch tunnel.

  • DC 12 Technology: Stabilize engines or shields.

  • DC 12 Perception: Identify incoming TIE fighters.

  • DC 13 Athletics: Manually hold or move damaged controls.

  • DC 12 Investigation: Reroute power.

  • DC 13 attack roll: Destroy debris or an obstruction.

  • DC 12 Medicine: Protect overloaded passengers during violent maneuvers.

Preparation Benefits

Apply automatic successes from:

  • Preparing the Stargazer

  • Bol’s repairs

  • Davik’s experienced crew

  • Recovered Imperial codes

  • Completing four or more evacuation objectives

Success

The Stargazer clears Bracken’s Point before the final orbital strike.

Failure

The ship still launches, but choose two complications:

  • The shields fail.

  • One engine is damaged.

  • Several passengers are injured.

  • The Imperial tracker remains attached.

  • A TIE fighter follows the ship into the upper atmosphere.

  • The NaviComputer loses part of its route data.

  • The ship suffers a hull breach.

  • A named ally is separated during launch.

The adventure continues.

20. The Last View of Velsar

The Stargazer rises above the industrial basin.

Bracken’s Point burns below.

Green fire descends from the Star Destroyer in measured lines, striking the Foundry Ward, Landing Yard, and outer settlements. Roads vanish beneath expanding clouds of dust. Towers fold into the basin, and the shift bells fall silent one by one.

Smaller lights move between the explosions—civilian transports, mining craft, and speeders carrying whoever managed to escape.

Then the clouds close beneath the ship.

Velsar disappears from view.

The party may have saved many people, but the destruction should still feel costly.

21. Crossing the Interdiction Field

The Imperial NaviComputer identifies a temporary weakness in the interdiction perimeter.

The characters must reach the calculated hyperspace point while avoiding pursuit.

With the Complete Navigation Key

The ship requires three successes before two failures.

Possible checks include:

  • DC 13 Piloting: Follow the precise route.

  • DC 12 Technology: Maintain the NaviComputer connection.

  • DC 13 Perception: Track Imperial ships.

  • DC 12 Deception: Broadcast false military credentials.

  • DC 13 attack roll: Drive off a pursuing fighter.

Success allows the Stargazer to enter hyperspace safely.

Failure causes the ship to take damage but still reach the jump point.

Without the Final Key

The route is incomplete.

The challenge requires four successes before two failures, and all DCs increase by 2.

On failure, Davik must make a blind hyperspace jump.

The Stargazer escapes but emerges:

  • In an unknown system

  • Near an Imperial patrol route

  • Inside a dangerous debris field

  • Far from Davik’s intended destination

  • With severe hyperdrive damage

Without the NaviComputer

If the party surrendered or lost the core, the Stargazer cannot safely cross the interdiction field through normal means.

Possible alternatives include:

  • Following an Imperial vessel through the field

  • Hiding among debris from Velsar

  • Using Voss’s command codes

  • Destroying an interdiction relay

  • Making a blind hyperspace jump

  • Allowing Tovan to guide Davik through the Force

Any such attempt should carry a serious consequence but should not automatically destroy the ship.

22. Determining the Survivors

Review completed objectives, rescued NPCs, and Community Support.

Zero or One Objective Completed

Only the Stargazer and scattered independent vessels escape.

Bracken’s Point is almost entirely destroyed.

Davik’s planetary organization collapses, and the survivors blame themselves and one another for those left behind.

Two Objectives Completed

A limited number of residents escape aboard transports or reach shelters outside the main target zone.

The community survives in fragments.

The characters are remembered as people who tried, though the losses remain severe.

Three Objectives Completed

Hundreds or thousands of civilians survive through tunnels, wilderness routes, and evacuation craft.

Davik’s network remains damaged but functional.

Stories of the characters spread among Velsar’s survivors.

Four Objectives Completed

Most organized evacuation groups reach shelter or escape craft.

Doctor Vey, Davik’s crew, neighborhood leaders, and important allies survive.

Bracken’s Point is destroyed, but its community remains coherent.

Five or More Objectives Completed

The characters achieve the best possible outcome.

The shift bells coordinate a widespread evacuation while smugglers, haulers, and workers move civilians beyond the bombardment zone.

Velsar suffers catastrophic destruction, but much of its population survives.

The Empire’s attempt to erase the settlement instead creates a mobile community of witnesses.

23. Tovan’s Fate

Tovan Escapes

Tovan becomes a mentor, ally, or reluctant passenger aboard the Stargazer.

He remains deeply affected by Velsar’s destruction but believes he must help the survivors find safety.

Tovan Sacrifices Himself

Tovan remains behind to draw Imperial fire or hold open an escape route.

The party sees a distant lightsaber or senses a sudden absence before the final strike.

His death is not definitively confirmed unless the characters witnessed it directly.

Tovan Is Captured

Voss transfers Tovan to the Star Destroyer before the bombardment.

The campaign can continue with a prison rescue or pursuit of the Imperial vessel.

Tovan Surrenders Voluntarily

His surrender delays the bombardment and may save an additional evacuation group.

Voss still enacts the contingency once Tovan is secured.

Tovan’s Fate Is Unknown

Tovan disappears during the chaos.

Survivors later report seeing a hooded figure leading civilians through the hills.

24. Adventure Endings

The Velsar Exodus

The party completes at least three evacuation objectives and escapes with the NaviComputer.

The Stargazer carries refugees, allies, and evidence of the Imperial purge.

Davik must find a safe world willing to receive them.

Ashes and Survivors

The party escapes but saves only a small number of people.

The survivors are alive, but Bracken’s Point and Davik’s network are gone.

The characters must decide whether to hide, seek revenge, or rebuild.

The Imperial Bargain

The party surrenders Tovan or the NaviComputer in exchange for time.

Voss honors the immediate terms but sends Imperial forces after the Stargazer.

The survivors may question the party’s decision even if it saved lives.

The Hermit’s Sacrifice

Tovan dies or remains behind while the party escapes.

His sacrifice becomes the story that unites Velsar’s refugees.

The Last Transport

The Stargazer is destroyed or cannot launch.

The party seizes an Imperial transport, cargo vessel, or prisoner shuttle.

The escape is more dangerous, and Davik’s ship is lost, but the campaign continues.

Prisoners of the Empire

The party is defeated at the hangar.

Voss captures the characters but transports them offworld before the bombardment.

The next adventure begins aboard an Imperial prison vessel with Velsar burning below.

25. Rewards

The characters do not automatically advance to 5th level during this module, though the GM may award 5th level after the epilogue if the campaign continues immediately.

Possible rewards include:

  • Shared use or ownership of the BT-9 Stargazer

  • Davik Renn as a patron

  • Tovan Rell as an ally

  • Imperial command codes

  • Evidence of Contingency Cinderglass

  • The damaged Jedi lightsaber

  • Rustclaw or Imperial equipment

  • Favors owed by Velsar survivors

  • Access to Davik’s wider smuggling syndicate

  • A reputation among frontier resistance networks

The most important reward is the community the characters saved—or the responsibility they inherit for those they could not.

26. Continuing the Campaign

Possible follow-up adventures include:

Refugees Without a World

The Stargazer must find a safe destination while food, fuel, medical supplies, and space run dangerously low.

Voss’s Pursuit

If Voss survives, he leads a dedicated Imperial task force against the characters and Velsar’s refugees.

Rescue Tovan Rell

The Empire transports Tovan to a fortified interrogation site or an Inquisitorial facility.

The Syndicate’s Price

Davik’s superiors demand compensation for lost operations, stolen Imperial technology, and refugees occupying syndicate assets.

The Cinderglass Evidence

The characters possess proof that the Empire deliberately destroyed civilian settlements.

Rebel cells, criminal organizations, and Imperial Intelligence all want the data.

The NaviComputer’s Hidden Route

The stolen navigation package contains coordinates for a classified Imperial system not included in the original mission.

Rebuilding the Stargazer

The damaged BT-9 requires expensive repairs, replacement parts, and a secure shipyard.

Chapter Conclusion

Stars stretch across the cockpit as the Stargazer enters hyperspace.

For several moments, no one speaks.

Survivors fill the corridors behind the cockpit—wounded workers, frightened children, exhausted smugglers, and people carrying the few possessions they could save.

Davik keeps both hands on the controls.

“There will be Imperial warrants in every nearby system by morning.”

Beyond the cockpit, the old ship groans around its passengers.

Tovan, if present, watches the light of hyperspace.

“Then we should decide what we are running toward.”

Behind them, Velsar burns.

Ahead, the galaxy remains open.

Chapter 3: The Ghost in the Hills

The characters begin this chapter at 3rd level. While Davik Renn’s mechanics install the stolen NaviComputer aboard the Stargazer, the party searches for an overdue transport and its missing crew.

The investigation leads them to Tovan Rell, a Jedi survivor who has quietly protected Velsar’s people for years. The Empire’s search closes around the valley, forcing the characters to decide whether to conceal Tovan, convince him to flee, or use him as leverage against Commander Voss.

The characters advance to 4th level after rescuing Davik’s pilots, learning Tovan’s identity, and returning to Bracken’s Point.

Chapter Overview

The characters:

  1. Receive the missing-transport assignment from Davik.

  2. Fly into Velsar’s eastern wilderness.

  3. Locate and investigate the wreck.

  4. Recover evidence from a damaged protocol droid.

  5. Follow the rescued pilots’ trail.

  6. Find Tovan Rell’s concealed refuge.

  7. Learn that Tovan survived Order 66.

  8. Respond to an Imperial reconnaissance sweep.

  9. Decide whether Tovan leaves the wilderness.

  10. Return to an occupied Bracken’s Point.

  11. Discover that the Empire has authorized Velsar’s destruction.

  12. Advance to 4th level.

1. Beginning the Chapter

Davik’s technicians require several hours to integrate the NaviComputer with the Stargazer. If Keelo Venn joined the party or was rescued, he assists with the installation.

Davik provides the characters with a utility shuttle and the last known coordinates of the missing transport.

Davik’s Briefing

Davik expands a map of the eastern ridges across the workbench.

“The transport is the Wayfarer. Small cargo vessel, two-person crew. Jessa Korr and Bol Rannik.”

Two identification images appear beside the ship’s route.

“They were carrying medical supplies and replacement power cells to three outer settlements. Their last telemetry showed engine damage here.”

A marker flashes inside a remote basin.

“No distress call. No landing report. No demand for ransom.”

Davik looks toward the shuttle waiting beyond the hangar doors.

“Find the ship. Bring back my people. Then tell me who thought shooting at them was a sensible decision.”

Davik offers:

  • 500 credits for locating the transport.

  • 250 credits for each pilot returned alive.

  • 100 credits for recovering the cargo.

  • Free use of the utility shuttle.

  • Two medpacs and a portable survival kit.

Davik suspects raiders, a rival smuggling crew, or an Imperial customs patrol. He does not know Tovan exists.

The Missing Crew

Jessa Korr

Jessa is a human pilot in her early forties. She is practical, suspicious, and fiercely loyal to Davik’s crew.

She suffered a broken leg and significant blood loss during the crash.

Bol Rannik

Bol is a middle-aged Duros navigator and mechanic. He is talkative under normal circumstances but has suffered a concussion and several burns.

Both pilots are alive because Tovan reached the wreck shortly after it crashed.

2. Imperial Search Pressure

The characters’ earlier actions influence how rapidly the Empire closes in during this chapter.

Begin the chapter at Search Pressure 0, then add 1 for each applicable circumstance:

  • The party was clearly identified during the Bent Spanner ambush.

  • The NaviComputer’s tamper beacon remained active.

  • The party fought Imperial forces at the checkpoint.

  • The Rustclaw transmitter remained operational when the party escaped.

  • Commander Voss knows the identification code of Davik’s shuttle.

The starting Search Pressure cannot exceed 2.

Increase Search Pressure by 1 when:

  • The characters transmit an open distress signal.

  • The shuttle suffers a conspicuous crash or explosion.

  • The party uses repeated loud weapons in the wilderness.

  • The characters take a short rest after reaching the wreck.

  • A probe droid or Imperial soldier escapes.

  • Tovan openly uses his lightsaber.

  • The characters fail an important concealment check by 5 or more.

Search Pressure Effects

Pressure 0: Unnoticed

The characters have time to investigate without interference.

Pressure 1: Tracked Activity

Imperial traffic can be heard on local communication channels. The Empire knows an unidentified shuttle entered the region.

Pressure 2: Aerial Search

A probe droid or reconnaissance craft begins searching the eastern ridges.

Pressure 3: Ground Sweep

An Imperial investigation team enters the valley.

Pressure 4: Probable Jedi Contact

Commander Voss receives evidence that someone with unusual abilities is operating in the region.

Pressure 5: Confirmation

The Empire confirms Tovan’s identity. Preparations for the purge begin immediately.

The purge eventually proceeds regardless of the final Search Pressure, but lower pressure grants the party more preparation time in Chapter 4.

3. Flight into the Eastern Ridges

The utility shuttle is old but reliable. It has room for the party, both missing pilots, and a modest amount of cargo.

Departure Boxed Text

The hangar doors separate, revealing a narrow launch tunnel cut through the basin wall.

Davik’s shuttle rises from the platform and accelerates into the passage. For several seconds, rock and industrial supports rush past the cockpit.

Then the vessel emerges into daylight.

Bracken’s Point falls behind as the shuttle flies east over broken ridges, abandoned mine roads, and wind-scoured valleys. No settlements appear below—only scattered machinery and the occasional line of smoke rising from a distant work camp.

Aerial Navigation

Locating the Wayfarer requires two successes before two failures.

Characters may attempt:

  • DC 11 Wisdom (Perception): Spot wreckage, smoke, or disturbed terrain.

  • DC 11 Intelligence (Investigation): Reconstruct the ship’s final trajectory.

  • DC 11 Intelligence (Technology): Recover fragments of its telemetry.

  • DC 10 Piloting: Follow the safest search pattern through the basin.

  • DC 12 Wisdom (Survival): Identify terrain suitable for an emergency landing.

A character cannot use the same skill twice during the challenge.

Two Successes

The characters locate the wreck and land nearby without attracting attention.

One Failure

The shuttle passes through a hazardous canyon. One character must succeed on a DC 11 Piloting check or the shuttle takes superficial damage.

Two Failures

The characters still locate the wreck, but the landing damages the shuttle’s repulsor assembly. Repairing it later requires a successful DC 12 Technology check.

Search Pressure also increases by 1.

4. The Wreck of the Wayfarer

Use the Crashed Transport Site battlemap.

Approach Boxed Text

A trail of blackened stone cuts across the basin floor.

At its end, a transport rests against the base of a cliff, its forward hull crushed and one wing partially buried beneath shattered rock. Long streaks of blaster scoring cross the vessel’s upper surface.

The rear cargo ramp hangs open.

No smoke rises from the wreck, and no one answers the shuttle’s approach.

The Wayfarer was attacked by an Imperial reconnaissance flight after its crew refused an unscheduled inspection. The pilots feared the Empire would confiscate their undocumented medical cargo and identify Davik’s network.

The attack disabled the engines and communications array. Jessa managed to crash-land the ship inside the basin.

Tovan observed the crash from the hills and rescued both pilots before Imperial personnel arrived.

5. Keyed Wreck Areas

Area 1: Impact Trail

The approach contains scorched stone, pieces of hull plating, and several long grooves carved by the transport’s landing gear.

A successful DC 11 Intelligence (Investigation) or Wisdom (Survival) check reveals:

  • The ship remained under control during most of the descent.

  • The damage occurred before impact.

  • The attacks came from above and behind.

  • The transport was struck by military-grade energy weapons.

A character proficient with vehicles or starships recognizes the pattern as consistent with TIE weapon fire.

Area 2: Cargo Compartment

The cargo compartment contains ruptured crates and broken restraint straps.

Most of the medical cargo is still present, but several emergency supplies are missing.

Characters find:

  • Three intact medical supply crates.

  • Two replacement power cells.

  • A portable repulsor stretcher missing from its rack.

  • Blood leading toward the forward compartment.

  • Drag marks leading out through the cargo ramp.

  • No signs of looting.

A successful DC 10 Wisdom (Medicine) check determines that at least one injured person was treated inside the ship before being moved.

Area 3: Crew Compartment

The crew compartment contains two empty bunks, personal storage, and a small galley.

The characters can recover:

  • Jessa’s flight jacket.

  • Bol’s toolkit.

  • A concealed hold containing 150 credits in contraband medical stimulants.

  • A damaged comlink tuned to Davik’s network.

  • A half-written message warning that an Imperial patrol was following them.

The characters may take the stimulants, though Davik notices if the sealed cargo has been opened.

Area 4: Cockpit

The cockpit is stained with blood and scattered fragments of transparisteel.

One pilot’s seat has been cut loose from its emergency restraints. The other is surrounded by discarded bandages and an empty injector.

A protocol droid lies against the rear bulkhead, its torso crushed and its photoreceptors dark.

A successful DC 11 Intelligence (Investigation) check reveals that someone entered after the crash and treated the pilots.

The cockpit controls also show that the Wayfarer was jammed during the attack.

A successful DC 12 Technology check recovers a partial sensor record showing two fast-moving Imperial craft approaching before the recording ends.

Area 5: The Protocol Droid

The damaged protocol droid is designated C4-V3, commonly called “Cavi.”

Its memory core remains partially functional.

A character may remove the core without a check. Recovering the stored recording requires a DC 12 Intelligence (Technology) check.

Another character may assist by stabilizing the droid’s power supply.

Successful Recovery

Static fills the display.

The recording shows the cockpit shortly after the crash. Jessa is unconscious, while Bol struggles to release his restraints.

A hooded human climbs through the damaged cockpit window.

“Do not move,” the stranger says. “You are both badly hurt.”

Bol reaches for a blaster.

The weapon slides across the cockpit floor before his hand reaches it.

The stranger pauses, apparently realizing what he has done.

He then cuts through Jessa’s restraint with a small metal device and begins treating her wounds.

The final image shows both pilots being loaded onto a weathered speeder. The hooded man drives east.

The recording ends.

A character who studies the recording and succeeds on a DC 12 Intelligence (Lore) check recognizes the metal device as a lightsaber hilt.

Failed Recovery

The characters obtain only fragmented images:

  • A hooded human.

  • One of the pilots being carried.

  • A speeder moving east.

  • An unidentified metal cylinder.

The droid’s directional log still indicates the speeder’s route.

Area 6: Exterior Tracks

Tracks outside the transport show that a speeder left the basin heading east.

The trail can be followed with:

  • DC 10 Wisdom (Survival) from the ground.

  • DC 13 Wisdom (Perception) from the air.

  • Automatic success if the protocol droid’s directional log was recovered.

A failed check does not lose the trail. Instead, the characters take longer and Search Pressure increases by 1.

6. Optional Complication: Imperial Investigators

If Search Pressure reaches 3 before the characters leave the wreck, an Imperial investigation team arrives.

Use:

  • 1 Imperial investigator

  • 2 stormtroopers

The team lands outside the basin or approaches aboard a patrol speeder.

They do not initially know the characters are involved with the NaviComputer.

Imperial Hail

A mechanical voice sounds over the shuttle’s receiver.

“Unidentified personnel at crash site Aurek-Seven, remain in place. This area is under Imperial investigation.”

A second voice follows, calm and precise.

“Secure your weapons and prepare identification.”

The characters can attempt to avoid combat.

Possible approaches include:

  • DC 12 Charisma (Deception): Pose as rescue contractors.

  • DC 12 Charisma (Persuasion): Claim Davik’s authority as the vessel’s owner.

  • DC 13 Technology: Alter the shuttle’s registration.

  • Conceal themselves and leave through the rocks with a DC 11 group Stealth check.

  • Depart before the patrol lands with a successful DC 11 Piloting check.

On a failed social check, the investigator orders the characters detained for questioning.

If combat occurs, the investigator attempts to collect evidence and withdraw rather than fight to the death.

Allowing the investigator or a trooper to escape increases Search Pressure by 1.

7. The Broken Beacon

The characters may detect a second signal while following the speeder trail.

This is the beacon from Tovan’s escape pod, which crashed on Velsar shortly after Order 66.

Investigating it is optional and takes approximately thirty minutes.

Beacon Boxed Text

A faint signal pulses from a narrow ravine north of the trail.

Beneath layers of dust and windblown debris lies the broken shell of an escape pod. Most of its markings have faded, but the scorched emblem of the Galactic Republic remains visible beneath the dirt.

The pod contains:

  • Republic-era medical supplies.

  • A damaged survival kit.

  • A scorched utility belt.

  • A cracked data chip.

  • Evidence that someone survived the crash.

A successful DC 12 Technology check recovers the following information from the data chip:

  • Passenger: Jedi Knight Tovan Rell.

  • Vessel: Republic medical cruiser Resolute Mercy.

  • Emergency launch date: shortly after the establishment of the Empire.

  • Status: missing and presumed dead.

Recovering this information grants advantage on the party’s first social check with Tovan.

Investigating the beacon increases Search Pressure by 1 unless the characters concealed their shuttle.

8. Finding Tovan’s Refuge

Tovan’s refuge lies beneath an overhanging shelf of rock overlooking a narrow valley.

Searching from the Air

Spotting the refuge from the shuttle requires a DC 15 Wisdom (Perception) check.

On a failure, the characters detect the speeder tracks but must land and continue on foot.

Searching from the Ground

Characters following the tracks locate the refuge with a DC 10 Wisdom (Survival or Perception) check.

On a failure, they locate the entrance after encountering one of Tovan’s warning markers. Tovan knows they are coming and waits outside.

9. Tovan’s Hidden Refuge

Use the Tovan Rell’s Hidden Refuge battlemap.

The refuge consists of a concealed exterior shelter, several shallow caves, a treatment chamber, and an escape route through the rear cliffs.

Exterior Boxed Text

At first, the rock shelf appears empty.

Then the shapes begin to resolve: camouflage netting painted to match the stone, a narrow doorway beneath the overhang, water collectors hidden among the rocks, and the outline of a battered speeder beneath a canvas cover.

A row of small metal chimes hangs near the entrance.

None of them move, though the wind is blowing.

Tovan has already detected the characters.

Unless they approach with obvious hostility, he allows them to enter.

10. Keyed Refuge Areas

Area 1: Camouflaged Approach

The path contains simple warning devices made from wire, scrap metal, and suspended stones.

They are alarms rather than traps.

A character can identify them with a DC 11 Wisdom (Perception) check. Avoiding them grants advantage on the party’s first Stealth check inside the refuge, though Tovan still senses living creatures approaching.

Area 2: Treatment Chamber

Jessa and Bol rest on improvised medical beds.

Two injured spacers lie beneath thermal blankets in a clean but primitive treatment area.

A hooded man kneels beside one of them, adjusting a medical monitor assembled from several incompatible devices.

He looks toward the entrance without surprise.

“Your friends are alive. The woman needs surgery. The Duros needs rest.”

His gaze moves across your weapons.

“Neither will benefit from violence.”

Jessa is unconscious but stable.

Bol is awake and can confirm:

  • Their ship was attacked by two TIE fighters.

  • Their communications were jammed.

  • Tovan rescued them.

  • Tovan moved objects without touching them.

  • Tovan asked no questions about their cargo or employer.

Area 3: Common Room

The common room contains a cooking unit, old blankets, repaired tools, maps, and records of people Tovan has helped.

The records refer to:

  • Missing miners found alive.

  • Injured travelers treated anonymously.

  • Predators driven away from settlements.

  • Supplies quietly delivered after storms.

  • Children rescued from a collapsed habitation block.

Several incidents are familiar local stories attributed to luck, spirits, or an unknown wanderer.

A character who succeeds on a DC 11 Wisdom (Insight) check realizes that Tovan has been protecting Velsar for years without taking credit.

Area 4: Workshop

The workshop contains mechanical parts, medical tools, and salvaged equipment.

A damaged Republic insignia has been turned face-down beneath a workbench.

Characters also find cloth matching the fabric discovered at the Desert Shrine, if that quest was completed.

A successful DC 12 Investigation check reveals a concealed panel behind a storage shelf.

Tovan does not stop characters from searching, but his attitude worsens if they do so without permission.

Area 5: Hidden Compartment

The compartment contains:

  • A damaged lightsaber.

  • Folded remnants of Jedi robes.

  • A Republic medical officer’s badge.

  • A compact holoprojector.

  • A sealed record naming Tovan Rell.

The lightsaber’s focusing assembly is unstable. It functions but may fail if used extensively.

Finding the compartment confirms Tovan’s identity.

Area 6: Meditation Alcove

The alcove overlooks the valley through a narrow opening in the rock.

It contains no furniture, only a worn blanket and several carefully arranged stones.

Force-sensitive characters feel a quiet presence here, accompanied by grief, restraint, and persistent vigilance.

A character who completes a brief meditation may make a DC 11 Wisdom saving throw. On a success, the character senses that Imperial forces are approaching before the refuge’s alarms activate.

Area 7: Rear Escape Passage

A narrow passage leads through the rock and emerges on the opposite side of the ridge.

The route is difficult for an injured creature but provides a concealed escape from the refuge.

A character may collapse the entrance with a successful DC 12 Technology or Athletics check after everyone passes through.

11. Meeting the Hermit

Tovan initially introduces himself only as Rell, a former battlefield medic.

He does not lie about rescuing the pilots but avoids discussing his past.

Tovan’s Initial Attitude

Tovan begins cautious.

His attitude improves when the characters:

  • Prioritize the pilots’ safety.

  • Return medical supplies from the transport.

  • Recovered his escape-pod data without threatening him.

  • Protected the Desert Shrine.

  • Speak respectfully about the Jedi.

  • Warn him about Imperial patrols.

  • Offer to move the pilots without exposing his refuge.

His attitude worsens when the characters:

  • Threaten him.

  • Search his belongings without permission.

  • Suggest selling him to the Empire.

  • Treat the pilots as secondary to their reward.

  • Attempt to take his lightsaber.

  • Reveal that they led Imperial forces directly to the refuge.

Exposing Tovan’s Identity

Tovan admits the truth if:

  • The characters recovered the data from the Broken Beacon.

  • They discover his lightsaber.

  • Bol describes what Tovan did during the rescue.

  • A character directly identifies him and succeeds on a DC 12 Persuasion check.

  • Imperial troops arrive.

  • The party has earned at least 2 Community Support.

Tovan’s Revelation

The hermit remains silent for several seconds.

Then he removes his hood.

“My name is Tovan Rell.”

He places the damaged metal cylinder on the table between you.

“I served the Jedi Order. I was a knight, not the master described in the rumors.”

He looks toward the injured pilots.

“I survived when many better people did not. Since then, I have tried to ensure that survival meant something.”

12. Tovan’s Story

Tovan served aboard the Republic medical cruiser Resolute Mercy during the Clone Wars.

When Order 66 was issued, the clones aboard the vessel attacked the Jedi healers and guardians assigned to it. Tovan escaped aboard a damaged pod while the cruiser burned.

He crashed on Velsar and was found by local workers. Those workers concealed him from the first Imperial search teams.

Tovan has remained in the wilderness ever since.

He does not believe the Empire came to Velsar solely because of him. The stolen NaviComputer caused the initial escalation. However, he understands that his discovery gives Voss justification to use far greater force.

Tovan refuses to blame the party.

“The Empire does not need a reason to be cruel. It needs only something it can call permission.”

13. The Choice Before the Sweep

Tovan believes the characters should take the pilots and leave him behind.

He intends to move deeper into the hills and draw Imperial attention away from Bracken’s Point.

The characters may attempt to convince him otherwise.

Convincing Tovan to Leave

A character may make a DC 13 Charisma (Persuasion) check.

The check is made with advantage if:

  • The party completed the Desert Shrine.

  • The party recovered the Broken Beacon.

  • The characters have at least 2 Community Support.

  • They argue that remaining will not protect Velsar.

  • They offer a concrete evacuation plan.

On a success, Tovan agrees to accompany the party or meet them near Davik’s hangar later.

On a failure, he refuses for now but may reconsider during the Imperial attack.

14. The Imperial Sweep

The sweep begins when Search Pressure reaches 3 or after the characters finish speaking with Tovan.

The force consists of:

  • 1 Imperial investigator

  • 3 stormtroopers

  • 1 probe droid or reconnaissance drone

The patrol has orders to locate the missing pilots, identify the person who rescued them, and capture witnesses alive.

Warning

One of the metal chimes outside rings once.

Tovan immediately looks toward the entrance.

A second chime sounds farther down the valley.

Then the low mechanical hum of a probe droid carries between the rocks.

Tovan rises.

“They followed you—or they followed me.”

He looks toward the pilots.

“Either way, we are out of time.”

15. Objectives During the Sweep

The encounter is not simply a battle to eliminate every Imperial.

The party must address three objectives:

Evacuate the Pilots

Jessa cannot move without assistance. Bol can walk at half speed if supported.

The repulsor stretcher can carry Jessa, but activating it requires an action.

Prevent a Transmission

The probe droid begins recording when it sees Tovan or detects Force activity.

At the end of its third turn after obtaining evidence, it transmits the recording to Commander Voss.

A character can:

  • Destroy the droid.

  • Jam it with a DC 13 Technology check.

  • Block its line of sight.

  • Lure it into the cave.

  • Damage its transmitter separately.

Preserve the Escape Route

The party must keep access to the shuttle, speeder, or rear passage open.

If Imperial troops reach the shuttle, they attempt to disable it rather than destroy it.

16. Approaches to the Sweep

Concealment

If Search Pressure is 3 or lower, the party may attempt to hide Tovan and the pilots.

This requires three successes before two failures using:

  • Stealth

  • Deception

  • Technology

  • Survival

  • Medicine

  • Insight

The base DC is 12.

Success causes the patrol to search the refuge without finding definitive evidence. The party can then leave after the Imperials move farther into the valley.

Failure begins combat with the investigator positioned near the refuge entrance.

Misdirection

The characters may send the patrol toward a false trail.

A successful DC 13 Survival or Deception check draws half the Imperial force away.

On a failure, the patrol discovers the deception and Search Pressure increases by 1.

Negotiation

The investigator may be convinced that Tovan is merely a wilderness medic.

This requires a DC 14 Charisma (Deception) check.

The check gains advantage if:

  • Tovan’s lightsaber remains concealed.

  • The probe droid has not recorded Force use.

  • The characters present legitimate rescue credentials.

  • Jessa or Bol supports the story.

  • The characters possess falsified medical records.

On a failure, the investigator orders Tovan detained.

Combat

The terrain favors the defenders.

Characters can use:

  • Rock formations as half or three-quarters cover.

  • Elevated ledges.

  • The narrow refuge entrance.

  • Loose stone that can be dropped onto a path.

  • The rear escape passage.

  • The camouflaged speeder.

  • The shuttle’s exterior lights or engines as distractions.

Imperial troops use stun settings unless Tovan activates his lightsaber.

Once a lightsaber is visible, they switch to lethal fire and prioritize transmitting evidence.

17. Tovan as an Ally

Tovan should support the characters without resolving the encounter for them.

Once per round, he performs one of the following:

  • Grants a character Force Guidance.

  • Moves a threatened character up to 20 feet.

  • Stabilizes or heals an injured character.

  • Deflects a blaster shot.

  • Pushes one enemy away from a pilot.

  • Holds open or collapses part of the escape route.

  • Distracts the probe droid.

Tovan uses his lightsaber only when:

  • A pilot is about to be killed.

  • A character is reduced to 0 hit points.

  • The rear passage is blocked.

  • The characters directly ask him to stand with them.

  • His identity has already been confirmed.

If Tovan activates his lightsaber, increase Search Pressure by 1 unless the probe droid and all Imperial witnesses are prevented from escaping.

18. Failure and Capture

The encounter should not end the adventure if the characters are defeated.

Partial Defeat

If the party retreats without the pilots, Tovan attempts to save them. Davik later asks the party to rescue the prisoners during The Prisoner Transfer.

Tovan Captured

Tovan surrenders if doing so prevents the execution of a character or civilian.

This changes Chapter 4. The party must decide whether to rescue him during the evacuation or use his capture to buy time.

Party Captured

The characters are transported toward Bracken’s Point with the injured pilots.

Davik’s network intercepts the convoy, or the party gains an opportunity to escape when Tovan disrupts the transport without revealing his position.

Imperial Team Eliminated

The Empire loses contact with the patrol and assumes it encountered armed resistance.

Search Pressure increases by 1, but Voss lacks definitive proof unless the probe droid transmitted evidence.

19. Leaving the Refuge

The party must decide what happens to Tovan.

Tovan Accompanies the Party

Tovan travels concealed aboard the shuttle or follows on his speeder.

Advantages:

  • He is available during the evacuation.

  • He can treat Jessa during the journey.

  • Davik gains direct knowledge of the threat.

Complications:

  • The Empire focuses more heavily on Davik’s network.

  • Hiding Tovan inside Bracken’s Point becomes difficult.

  • Search Pressure increases by 1 if the shuttle was tracked.

Tovan Remains in the Wilderness

Tovan relocates to another shelter and begins warning remote settlements.

Advantages:

  • He can organize wilderness survivors during the purge.

  • The Empire has greater difficulty locating Davik’s hangar.

Chapter 2: The Rustclaw Revel

The characters begin this chapter at 2nd level. They must infiltrate an abandoned ore-processing compound, recover the Imperial authentication wafer, reclaim anything lost during the ambush, and survive a confrontation with Ressik.

This chapter is designed as an infiltration rather than a single large battle. The Rustclaws outnumber the party, but they are scattered, intoxicated, divided in loyalty, and unprepared for an organized attack.

The characters advance to 3rd level after assembling the complete NaviComputer and delivering it to Davik Renn.

Chapter Overview

The characters:

  1. Gather information and prepare for the operation.

  2. Travel through the hills beyond Bracken’s Point.

  3. Reconnoiter the Rustclaw compound.

  4. Infiltrate, deceive, or assault the gang.

  5. Recover the authentication wafer and any other stolen objectives.

  6. Confront Ressik.

  7. Escape before the Empire or additional Rustclaws arrive.

  8. Return through a newly established Imperial checkpoint.

  9. Meet Davik Renn and receive payment.

  10. Accept a job investigating his missing transport.

1. Beginning the Chapter

Tensin provides the characters with the approximate location of the Rustclaw hideout: an abandoned ore-processing station built into a rocky ridge several miles southeast of Bracken’s Point.

What the characters must recover depends on the outcome of Chapter 1.

Previous OutcomeRequired Objective
