The authentication wafer is always in Ressik’s possession when the characters arrive.

Tensin’s Briefing

Tensin spreads a stained industrial survey across the workbench.

“The station was abandoned after the southern ore seam collapsed. Ressik moved in because it has walls, power, and only three routes of approach.”

He taps several faded structures on the map.

“The Rustclaws use the yard for stolen vehicles, the upper buildings for sleeping quarters, and the old control hall for Ressik’s throne room—or whatever he calls it.”

He looks around at the group.

“There are too many to fight all at once. Fortunately, most of them have been drinking since yesterday.”

Tensin knows the following:

  • Approximately a dozen Rustclaws use the compound.

  • Two lookouts normally watch the approaches.

  • Ressik keeps valuable trophies near him.

  • The gang has been celebrating since the ambush.

  • A stolen speeder is undergoing repairs in the vehicle yard.

  • The station’s alarm, doors, and lighting still connect to an old control network.

  • Rustclaw loyalty to Ressik is based primarily on fear.

Tensin recommends stealth, sabotage, or deception. He does not accompany the party unless the characters must rescue someone he personally cares about.

2. Preparing in Bracken’s Point

The characters may depart immediately or spend several hours gathering information and equipment.

They can complete town side quests before leaving. Each completed quest grants 1 point of Community Support and may provide an advantage during the infiltration.

The Missing Mechanic

Completing this quest reveals that Pavo Nesh is being held in the hideout’s vehicle yard and forced to repair a stolen speeder.

If Pavo has already escaped or been rescued, he provides:

  • The location of a damaged rear fence.

  • The general layout of the vehicle yard.

  • A description of the gang’s escape speeder.

  • Advantage on one check made to sabotage a vehicle or machine inside the compound.

The Street Doc’s Dilemma

A wounded Rustclaw reveals:

  • The name of the current gate password.

  • The location of the slicer station.

  • Ressik’s habit of demanding personal challenges.

  • Which gang members resent Ressik.

The current gate password is “Final Claim.”

Trouble at the Cantina

Sella Vorn can provide:

  • A suppressed blaster power regulator.

  • Directions to an old mining trail.

  • A distraction staged near the western approach.

  • A promise to collect anyone who escapes the compound on foot.

Purchasing Equipment

Tensin can obtain the following items at normal cost:

  • Medpacs

  • Restraints

  • Glow rods

  • Climbing equipment

  • Smoke grenades

  • Comlinks

  • Basic slicing tools

  • Two doses of stimulant neutralizer

The stimulant neutralizer removes the intoxicated penalties from one creature for 1 hour. Tensin claims it was intended for “medical emergencies involving poor judgment.”

3. Journey to the Hideout

The compound lies approximately four hours from Bracken’s Point on foot or one hour by speeder.

The terrain consists of broken ridges, dry gullies, abandoned mining roads, and patches of thorny scrub.

Wilderness Boxed Text

Bracken’s Point disappears behind the ridges within the first hour.

The road narrows into two weathered tracks winding through rust-colored stone. Old mining pylons lean above the ravines, their cables long since stripped away. Wind moves through empty excavation cuts and carries the distant rattle of loose metal.

Ahead, smoke rises from somewhere beyond the next ridge.

Choosing an Approach

The characters may approach through one of three routes.

The Old Mining Road

The fastest and most obvious route.

  • No travel check is required.

  • The party reaches the main gate.

  • The exterior lookouts automatically notice any approaching vehicle.

  • Characters using the gate password may attempt to bluff their way inside.

The Western Ravine

A narrow route concealed by rock formations.

The party must succeed on a DC 11 group Wisdom (Survival) check.

On a success, the party reaches the rear fence unnoticed.

On a failure, one character suffers 3 (1d6) kinetic damage from a fall or loose rock, and the party arrives after nightfall. The darkness helps conceal them, but the gang has posted an additional lookout.

The Upper Ridge

A difficult climbing route overlooking the compound.

Each character must succeed on a DC 10 Strength (Athletics) check. Characters with climbing equipment have advantage.

A character who fails takes 3 (1d6) kinetic damage but still completes the ascent.

From the ridge, the characters can observe most of the exterior compound and identify patrol routes before descending.

4. Reconnoitering the Compound

Use the Ressik’s Rustclaw Hideout battlemap.

Allow the characters to observe the compound before entering.

Exterior Description

The old processing station fills a natural shelf between the cliffs.

Scrap-metal walls surround a broad vehicle yard littered with machinery, cargo containers, and dismantled speeders. Watch platforms overlook the main gate and western fence. A large industrial building occupies the eastern half of the compound, its upper windows glowing with uneven yellow light.

Music and shouting carry across the yard.

Someone fires a blaster into the air. Several voices cheer.

A character who spends at least 10 minutes observing the hideout and succeeds on a DC 11 Wisdom (Perception) or Intelligence (Investigation) check learns two facts from the following list. Reveal one fact on a failed check.

  • Two fighters guard the exterior approaches.

  • Most gang members are gathered in the drinking hall.

  • The vehicle yard contains several usable speeders.

  • The western fence is damaged.

  • The upper control room has a direct view of the yard.

  • Power conduits run from an exterior generator into the main building.

  • One guard repeatedly leaves his post to obtain drinks.

  • A prisoner or mechanic is working inside the vehicle shelter.

5. Rustclaw Alert Level

The compound’s response is governed by an Alert Level.

Begin at Alert 0 unless the party approached openly or previously allowed the Rustclaws time to prepare.

Alert 0: Unaware

The gang is drinking, gambling, sleeping, and celebrating.

  • Lookouts remain at their assigned positions.

  • Interior doors are unlocked.

  • Rustclaws have disadvantage on their first attack roll and first saving throw in combat.

  • Loud noises are dismissed unless repeated.

Alert 1: Suspicious

The gang believes something may be wrong.

  • A fighter investigates unusual sounds.

  • Exterior doors are closed but not locked.

  • Lookouts begin actively searching.

  • Characters have disadvantage on checks made to impersonate Rustclaws without a convincing disguise.

Alert 2: Mobilized

The compound knows intruders are present.

  • Doors are locked.

  • The bruisers begin organizing defenders.

  • One fighter attempts to reach the slicer station.

  • Ressik remains in his hall and demands information.

Alert 3: Full Alarm

The entire compound is responding.

  • Remaining Rustclaws move toward defensible positions.

  • The escape speeder is prepared.

  • Ressik moves toward the drinking hall or vehicle yard.

  • A message is sent to gang associates near Bracken’s Point.

Increase the Alert Level when:

  • A lookout escapes.

  • An alarm is activated.

  • A body is discovered.

  • A loud weapon is discharged repeatedly.

  • A character fails a Stealth check by 5 or more.

  • A Rustclaw is allowed to shout a warning.

  • The party drives through the main gate without permission.

Reducing the Alert Level is difficult, but characters can create false explanations, disable communications, or persuade Keelo to transmit an all-clear.

6. Compound Roster

The hideout contains:

  • Ressik

  • 10 Rustclaw fighters

  • 2 Rustclaw bruisers

  • Keelo Venn, if captured

  • Pavo Nesh, if not previously rescued

  • Tensin Black, if captured

  • One or two other civilian prisoners at the GM’s discretion

The enemies are distributed throughout the compound. They should never begin combat as one group.

Area 1: Main Gate

The main gate consists of two sliding scrap-metal barriers and a small guard station.

One Rustclaw fighter occupies the platform above the gate. A second periodically walks between the gate and the vehicle yard.

Bluffing Entry

Characters who know the password can make a DC 11 Charisma (Deception) check to gain entry.

A convincing disguise, captured gang vehicle, or restrained “prisoner” grants advantage.

On a failure, the guards demand that the characters disarm and wait while someone contacts Ressik. The Alert Level increases to 1.

Gate Controls

The gate can be sliced with a DC 11 Intelligence (Technology) check.

On a success, the character can open, close, or lock the gate. On a failure, the gate opens but the Alert Level increases by 1.

Area 2: Western Fence

A character can enter through the damaged section with a successful DC 10 Dexterity (Stealth) check. A character wearing heavy armor makes this check with disadvantage unless another character assists.

Area 3: Vehicle Yard

The vehicle yard contains:

Freeing Pavo

Pavo quietly cooperates with the characters.

The room reeks of spilled liquor, scorched meat, and machine oil.

No one appears prepared for a disciplined attack.

Four Rustclaw fighters occupy the room.

At Alert 0, two are seated, one is gambling, and one is asleep beneath a table.

The characters may cross the room without combat by:

  • Activate the ore lift.

Area 6: Barracks

The barracks contains stacked bunks, weapons lockers, and personal storage crates.

Two fighters and one bruiser are resting here.

At Alert 0, all three are asleep or heavily intoxicated. Characters who enter quietly can attempt to bypass them with a DC 10 group Stealth check.

A damaged coolant regulator runs along the rear wall.

  • One fragmentation grenade

This workshop contains repair benches, hanging chains, cutting tools, and a suspended engine assembly.

A character may:

  • Drop the engine assembly with a DC 11 Technology check.

  • Create a loud distraction.

  • Disable building power.

  • Construct an improvised trap.

  • Hide prisoners or civilians.

The engine hangs 15 feet above the floor.

A creature beneath it when released must make a DC 13 Dexterity saving throw, taking 14 (4d6) kinetic damage on a failed save or half as much on a success.

Area 8: Holding Room

The Rustclaws use an old equipment cage as a temporary holding room.

Tensin is held here if captured during Chapter 1. Otherwise, the room contains two civilian merchants detained for ransom.

The cage can be opened with:

  • A DC 12 Technology check.

  • 15 points of damage against its AC 15 door.

Area 9: Trophy Passage

The corridor outside Ressik’s hall displays weapons, armor fragments, skulls, hides, and scavenged insignia.

A character who studies the trophies and succeeds on a DC 12 Wisdom (Insight) or Intelligence (Lore) check realizes that Ressik’s reputation exceeds his actual accomplishments. Several trophies were purchased, stolen, or taken from already dead creatures.

A character who presents this evidence during the confrontation gains advantage on one Charisma check against the assembled Rustclaws.

The old control hall has been converted into a throne room assembled from industrial wreckage.

“There you are.”

  • Rustclaw account ledger

  • A collection of trophies worth 300 credits

8. Negotiating with Ressik

Ressik does not attack immediately unless the party has killed several gang members or publicly humiliated him.

He wants the characters to understand that they have entered his territory and must now entertain him.

Ressik may exchange the wafer for something that increases his status:

  • A valuable weapon

  • A promise of dangerous prey

  • Information damaging to Davik

  • Public recognition that Ressik defeated Tensin

  • A duel against a worthy opponent

  • Proof that keeping the device will bring overwhelming Imperial retaliation

Ordinary credits do not interest him unless the offer exceeds 1,000 credits.

Revealing the Imperial Threat

Characters who discovered the tamper beacon or Imperial interest can attempt to convince Ressik that the device is dangerous.

This requires a DC 13 Charisma (Persuasion or Deception) check.

The check is made with advantage if the characters possess:

  • Imperial records

  • Evidence of increased patrols

  • Keelo’s testimony

  • Information gained from an investigator

  • The active tamper beacon

On a success, Ressik agrees to surrender the wafer in exchange for the characters taking the core and accepting responsibility for it.

He still attempts to keep Tensin’s credits unless the party bargains for them separately.

9. Ressik’s Challenge

If a Wookiee character is present, Ressik immediately challenges that character.

Otherwise, he challenges whichever character appears physically strongest or has most openly defied him.

Duel Terms

The standard terms are:

  • No outside interference.

  • Melee weapons only.

  • The duel ends when one participant yields, falls unconscious, or is forced outside the marked area.

  • If the challenger wins, the party receives the wafer.

  • If Ressik wins, the party leaves the compound and surrenders one weapon of his choice.

The characters may negotiate additional stakes, including the core, prisoners, payment case, or safe passage.

Ressik’s Cheating

Ressik claims to value honorable combat but cheats if he believes he can conceal it.

At half hit points, he may:

  • Kick debris into his opponent’s face.

  • Activate a concealed shock module.

  • Signal a gang member to interfere.

  • Move outside the marked area and claim he was pushed.

A character observing the duel may notice the cheating with a DC 12 Wisdom (Perception) check.

Publicly exposing him forces Ressik to make a DC 12 Charisma check. On a failure, the gang refuses to interfere with the remainder of the duel.

10. Fighting Ressik

For four 2nd-level characters, Ressik should not fight beside every remaining gang member.

A standard boss encounter consists of:

  • Ressik

  • One Rustclaw bruiser

  • One Rustclaw fighter

Additional fighters arrive only if the compound is at Alert 3, normally one at the end of every other round.

Environmental Features

Ressik’s hall contains:

  • An elevated control platform

  • Hanging chains

  • A damaged coolant line

  • Tables and trophy racks providing half cover

  • A large viewport overlooking the yard

  • An industrial chair bolted to a rotating platform

A character can use an action and make an appropriate DC 11–13 check to:

  • Drop a trophy rack.

  • Rupture the coolant line.

  • Rotate the control platform.

  • Extinguish the lights.

  • Seal one entrance.

  • Broadcast the confrontation throughout the compound.

Gang Morale

The Rustclaws are loyal only while Ressik appears dominant.

The gang begins retreating or surrendering when two of the following occur:

  • Ressik is reduced below half hit points.

  • A bruiser is defeated.

  • The alarm system is disabled.

  • Keelo denounces Ressik over the intercom.

  • The party publicly reveals the fraudulent trophies.

  • Half of the fighters are incapacitated.

  • The party seizes the core and wafer.

  • Ressik cheats during a witnessed duel.

  • The escape vehicles are disabled.

If Ressik falls unconscious or yields, most surviving Rustclaws flee.

11. Alternative Outcomes

Ressik Is Killed

The Rustclaws fragment into smaller crews. Some flee Velsar, while others seek revenge or employment with Davik.

The Empire later describes Ressik’s death as evidence of escalating criminal violence.

Ressik Is Defeated but Spared

Ressik honors the immediate agreement but swears to reclaim his reputation.

He may become a recurring rival, reluctant ally, or future bounty hunter.

Ressik Is Publicly Humiliated

The Party Negotiates

The characters leave without a major battle. Ressik remains in power but understands that the Empire is closing in.

He begins evacuating his compound shortly afterward.

The Party Is Defeated

Ressik does not immediately kill them.

The characters awaken in the holding room, stripped of obvious weapons. Keelo, Tensin, Pavo, or a disloyal fighter helps them escape.

Their equipment is stored in the barracks, while the core and wafer remain in Ressik’s hall.

12. Escaping the Compound

Once the party acquires its objectives, it must leave before reinforcements or Imperial patrols arrive.

If the Alert Level is 0 or 1, the party can leave without a formal chase.

At Alert 2 or 3, use a short escape challenge requiring three successes before two failures.

Useful checks include:

  • Athletics: Climb a fence or force open a door.

  • Acrobatics: Cross machinery or descend a cliff.

  • Stealth: Evade pursuing Rustclaws.

  • Technology: Activate or disable a vehicle.

  • Piloting: Escape aboard a speeder.

  • Deception: Send pursuers toward the wrong exit.

  • Intimidation: Convince demoralized fighters to stand aside.

Success

The party escapes cleanly.

One Failure

A pursuit vehicle follows them into the hills.

Two Failures

The party escapes but loses one minor item, suffers 1d6 damage each, or leaves evidence identifying its route to Bracken’s Point.

13. Return to Bracken’s Point

The characters discover that the Imperial presence has expanded while they were away.

Checkpoint Boxed Text

Portable floodlights illuminate the road ahead.

Stormtroopers stand behind newly erected barricades while officers inspect civilian vehicles and compare faces against data records. A probe droid drifts above the waiting line.

The soldiers occasionally open cargo containers, but most of their questions concern wilderness shelters, missing travelers, and reports of unusual lights in the hills.

The checkpoint is searching for the rumored Jedi. Its personnel do not know the exact appearance of the NaviComputer.

  • DC 11 Intelligence (Technology): Forge a cargo manifest.

  • DC 11 Dexterity (Stealth): Bypass the road through the rocks.

  • A 100-credit bribe.

  • Imperial documentation acquired earlier.

  • A concealed compartment inside a vehicle.

If the characters rescued civilians, concealing everyone increases the relevant DC by 1.

Failure

An officer orders the vehicle aside for additional inspection.

The characters can:

  • Create a distraction.

  • Abandon the vehicle.

  • Hide the core before inspection.

  • Allow themselves to be questioned.

  • Use the side trail identified by Sella or Pavo.

Combat at the checkpoint is possible but should be presented as highly dangerous.

14. Meeting Davik Renn

Tensin leads the characters to Davik’s reclamation yard after they return.

A freight elevator descends beneath the surface facility into a concealed excavation chamber.

Hidden Hangar Boxed Text

The elevator descends through layers of stone and abandoned industrial supports.

A vast chamber opens below.

Work lights illuminate an aging starship resting within a forest of scaffolding. Its broad hull is covered in mismatched plates, old repairs, faded markings, and carbon scoring. Mechanics move beneath its landing gear while cables and fuel lines connect it to the surrounding platforms.

The ship is neither elegant nor new.

It looks difficult to kill.

An older man waits beside the boarding ramp, watching as the freight elevator reaches the hangar floor.

Davik Renn greets the party personally.

Completing the Deal

Davik’s slicers inspect the NaviComputer.

If the characters recovered both the core and wafer, the device is genuine and operational after several hours of work.

Davik pays:

  • The remainder of Tensin’s promised reward.

  • The additional 750-credit recovery bonus.

  • 100 credits for each civilian rescued from the Rustclaws.

  • A 250-credit bonus if the tamper beacon was disabled.

  • Fair value for any useful Imperial intelligence.

If the characters negotiated rather than destroyed the compound, Davik expresses approval. He prefers rivals who can still be useful later.

Davik’s Questions

Davik wants to know:

  • How the characters acquired the device.

  • Whether the Empire traced it.

  • Whether Ressik survived.

  • Whether Keelo can be trusted.

  • How many people know Davik was the buyer.

  • Whether the characters were identified at the checkpoint.

Davik does not punish imperfect outcomes. He evaluates whether the party tells the truth.

A character who succeeds on a DC 12 Wisdom (Insight) check realizes Davik already knows much of what happened and is measuring their honesty.

15. The Missing Transport

Davik’s mechanics need several hours to slice and install the device.

While they work, Davik offers the party another job.

Davik studies the restored navigation core before turning away from the workbench.

“A transport belonging to me missed two scheduled calls.”

He activates a map of the eastern ridges. A blinking marker appears in a remote basin.

“Two pilots. Medical cargo. No distress transmission, but their last telemetry showed engine damage.”

He looks toward the Stargazer.

“My people need time to install your prize. You need work. Find the transport and bring back whoever is still alive.”

Davik provides:

  • A utility shuttle

  • The transport’s last coordinates

  • Emergency medical supplies

  • A 500-credit recovery contract

  • An additional 250 credits for each surviving pilot

Davik believes raiders or Imperial patrols attacked the transport. He has no knowledge of Tovan Rell.

16. Chapter Conclusion

The characters advance to 3rd level after delivering the complete NaviComputer to Davik.

Mechanics carry the navigation core aboard the Stargazer as power returns to its outer systems.

One by one, running lights illuminate across the patched hull.

Beyond the hangar, distant sirens echo through Bracken’s Point.

Davik looks toward the sealed doors.

“Whatever is happening out there, it is moving faster than I expected.”

He hands you the shuttle’s access cylinder.

“Find my people. Then we decide how long Velsar remains safe.”

Chapter 3 begins with the flight to the missing transport’s last known position.

ASHES OF VELSAR

A Star Wars 5th Edition adventure for four characters of 1st–4th level

Era: Approximately 3–5 years after Order 66
Setting: The Mid Rim frontier world of Velsar
Themes: Community, occupation, survival, compromise, and resistance
Expected Length: 6–10 sessions
Working Planet Name: Velsar

Adventure Summary

The frontier world of Velsar has never mattered much to the Galactic Empire.

Its mines are poor, its factories outdated, and its settlements held together by welded scrap and stubborn labor. Imperial authority is represented by underpaid customs officials, neglected checkpoints, and inspectors who rarely leave their offices.

That changes when the Rustclaws, a violent salvage gang, steal an experimental Imperial NaviComputer containing interdiction telemetry and encrypted military access codes.

The characters are hired by a nervous fixer named Tensin Black to retrieve the device. What begins as a simple underworld job draws them into a conflict between the Rustclaws, the planetary smuggling network of Davik Renn, and an escalating Imperial investigation.

At the same time, rumors spread that a Jedi survivor has been hiding in Velsar’s wilderness.

When the Empire confirms those rumors, the search for the stolen NaviComputer becomes secondary. Imperial forces evacuate their installations, a Star Destroyer descends into low orbit, and Velsar is marked for eradication.

The characters must decide who they are willing to save, what they are willing to sacrifice, and whether they can escape aboard Davik Renn’s battered BT-9 Stargazer before fire falls from the sky.

OPENING CRAWL

STAR WARS

RUNNING THE ADVENTURE

Adventure Structure

The adventure is divided into four chapters.

Chapter 1: A Simple Job

The 1st-level characters arrive in Bracken’s Point, meet Tensin Black, and retrieve the stolen NaviComputer from a frightened gang slicer. A Rustclaw ambush and Imperial intervention leave the characters without the device or their payment.

The characters advance to 2nd level after surviving the ambush and agreeing to recover the NaviComputer.

Chapter 2: The Rustclaw Revel

The characters track the Rustclaws to a wilderness hideout where the gang is celebrating its apparent victory. They must infiltrate, negotiate with, or fight the gang and its Trandoshan leader, Ressik.

After recovering the NaviComputer and delivering it to Davik Renn, the characters advance to 3rd level.

Chapter 3: The Ghost in the Hills

While Davik’s people install the NaviComputer aboard the BT-9 Stargazer, the characters investigate a missing transport. The wreck leads them to a hermit who has secretly protected the people of Velsar for years.

The hermit is revealed as Tovan Rell, a Jedi survivor.

After meeting Tovan and surviving the Empire’s first major sweep, the characters advance to 4th level.

Chapter 4: Fire from the Sky

The Empire begins withdrawing from Velsar. A Star Destroyer assumes a low orbital position, and Commander Voss prepares a final attempt to capture Tovan and recover the NaviComputer.

When orbital bombardment begins, the characters must reach the Stargazer, save whoever they can, and escape the planet.

Milestone Advancement

Characters advance as follows:

  • Level 1: Arrival on Velsar

  • Level 2: Survive the Rustclaw ambush and Imperial intervention

  • Level 3: Recover the NaviComputer and complete the deal with Davik

  • Level 4: Discover the hermit’s identity and survive the Imperial sweep

Characters remain 4th level during the final evacuation.

Themes and Tone

The first half of the adventure should feel like a frontier crime story. The characters deal with fixers, gangs, smugglers, frightened civilians, and apathetic officials.

The second half becomes an occupation thriller. Checkpoints appear. Neighbors disappear. Stormtroopers begin searching homes. People lower their voices when patrols pass.

The final chapter is a disaster scenario. The objective is not to defeat the Empire. It is to survive, preserve what remains of the community, and escape before Velsar is destroyed.

VELSAR

A Penal Resettlement World

Velsar is officially classified as an Imperial penal resettlement and industrial reclamation colony.

It is not a conventional prison planet. Most of its population is free, and many families have lived there for generations. The Empire sends debtors, low-risk prisoners, political undesirables, and parole laborers to work alongside civilian miners and salvagers.

Once assigned to Velsar, few people earn enough to leave.

This arrangement allows player characters to arrive for many different reasons. A character might be:

  • A recently released prisoner

  • A contracted laborer

  • A spacer stranded by debt

  • A mercenary following a job lead

  • A local returning home

  • A fugitive using forged documents

  • A technician assigned to an industrial project

  • A traveler whose transport route ends on Velsar

The characters do not need to know one another before the adventure. Tensin Black has contacted each of them separately and arranged for them to meet after arrival.

Bracken’s Point

Bracken’s Point is the largest settlement on Velsar and the center of the adventure.

It is constructed around a deep industrial basin surrounded by scrapyards, low refineries, ore crushers, freight lifts, and modular housing blocks. Generations of repairs have left almost no original structure visible.

Buildings are reinforced with mismatched armor plates. Walkways cross above narrow streets. Power cables sag between rooftops. Steam vents from buried conduits, and the sound of machinery continues at all hours.

Common Sounds

  • Shift bells ringing across the settlement

  • Welding torches and power tools

  • Repulsor engines passing overhead

  • Metal striking metal

  • Wind moving through scaffolding

  • Distant ore processors

  • Public-address announcements distorted by old speakers

Community Values

People on Velsar respect useful work.

Mechanics, haulers, welders, engineers, medics, and salvagers carry more social influence than wealthy outsiders or appointed officials. Residents remember who helped during a shortage and who refused.

Outsiders are watched but not automatically rejected. A newcomer who works beside the locals can earn acceptance quickly.

Community Support

The characters’ actions during the adventure determine how much help Bracken’s Point provides during the final evacuation.

The party gains 1 point of Community Support whenever it completes a side quest in a way that meaningfully helps the people of Velsar.

Community Support has the following effects:

1 Point: Familiar Faces

Locals recognize the characters and are willing to hide them from routine patrols.

2 Points: Quiet Assistance

The characters have advantage on one group ability check made to move through Bracken’s Point during the lockdown.

3 Points: The Shift Bells

When the bombardment begins, the community uses the settlement’s shift bells to coordinate evacuations. The party can prevent one increase of the Purge Clock.

4 or More Points: Velsar Stands Together

Workers, smugglers, mechanics, and neighborhood watches organize a coordinated resistance. During the final chapter, one evacuation objective is automatically completed.

THE STOLEN NAVICOMPUTER

The stolen device is an IN-4 Imperial Interdiction Navigation Core.

It resembles a reinforced black cylinder approximately two feet long, covered in access ports and Imperial authentication seals.

The device does not allow a ship to ignore every Imperial interdiction field indefinitely. It contains:

  • Current Imperial interdiction telemetry

  • Classified patrol routes

  • Short-lived military identification codes

  • Algorithms for locating gaps in interdiction networks

  • Encrypted records of Imperial fleet deployments

  • A sealed emergency navigation package

When properly installed, the core can guide a ship through one active Imperial interdiction network before its authentication codes are invalidated.

Davik wants it because it could provide his organization with a secure escape route from Velsar.

Commander Voss wants it recovered because its disappearance exposes classified Imperial operations and threatens his command.

The Rustclaws stole it from an Imperial customs shipment without understanding its full importance.

MAJOR CHARACTERS

Tensin Black

Role: Fixer and unreliable patron
Disposition: Nervous, ambitious, fast-talking
Desire: To become indispensable to Davik Renn
Fear: Being abandoned when the Empire arrives
Secret: Tensin promised the NaviComputer to Davik before he actually possessed it

Tensin dresses better than most people in Bracken’s Point, though close inspection reveals repaired seams and imitation materials. He constantly checks exits, watches reflections, and lowers his voice even when no one appears to be listening.

Tensin is not courageous, but he is not needlessly cruel. When danger becomes real, his first instinct is to run. He might return later if guilt, profit, or self-preservation gives him sufficient reason.

Roleplaying Tensin: Speak quickly. Make assurances before anyone asks for them. Treat every setback as temporary until escape becomes necessary.

“This is not a dangerous job. Dangerous jobs pay much better. This is an inconvenient job with dangerous-looking people standing near it.”

Davik Renn

Role: Smuggling boss and potential long-term patron
Disposition: Patient, practical, weary
Desire: To keep his network alive without attracting sector-level attention
Fear: Becoming too important for the Empire to ignore
Secret: Davik’s planetary smuggling organization answers to a larger offworld syndicate

Davik is prominent on Velsar but is not a crime lord. He controls transporters, hidden landing sites, mechanics, and supply routes across the planet, but much of his wealth exists as favors, equipment, and obligations.

His greatest asset is the BT-9 Stargazer, an aging and heavily modified transport capable of reaching orbit and surviving routes that would destroy newer vessels.

Davik knows that he is an old man in a young person’s profession. He respects competence and dislikes unnecessary violence.

Roleplaying Davik: Speak slowly. Allow silence to make other people uncomfortable. Never threaten someone when a practical statement will accomplish the same purpose.

“Everyone believes smugglers are paid to carry cargo. We are paid to know when not to ask what the cargo is.”

Ressik

Role: Rustclaw gang boss
Species: Trandoshan
Disposition: Violent, theatrical, intoxicated
Desire: Respect through fear and trophies
Fear: Being dismissed as a common scavenger
Secret: Ressik stole the NaviComputer largely to embarrass Davik

Ressik is a massive, one-eyed Trandoshan who wears a mantle made from Wookiee hide. He despises Wookiees but considers them worthy opponents.

He is almost always drinking, but alcohol has little visible effect on his reflexes. He encourages his followers to drink heavily because it makes them easier to control.

If a Wookiee is present, Ressik demands a personal duel. He considers interference dishonorable but has no objection to cheating when he believes no one can prove it.

Roleplaying Ressik: Laugh loudly. Invade personal space. Treat negotiation as an opportunity to display dominance.

“Credits disappear. Machines break. A worthy kill stays with you.”

Tovan Rell, the Hermit

Role: Jedi survivor and moral center
Disposition: Quiet, compassionate, haunted
Desire: To protect Velsar without drawing attention to it
Fear: That every person he saves will eventually die because of him
Secret: Tovan was only a Jedi Knight when the Order fell; the title of Jedi Master is a rumor created by frightened locals

Tovan survived Order 66 when his transport was shot down over Velsar. He has lived in the wilderness ever since, moving between concealed shelters and avoiding populated settlements.

Over the years, he has rescued lost workers, treated injuries, redirected predators, and intervened in accidents without revealing his identity.

He carries a damaged lightsaber but rarely activates it. Its focusing assembly is unstable, and prolonged use risks destroying the weapon.

Tovan does not want the characters to fight the Empire for him. He believes Velsar’s people will suffer if he remains, but leaving may require abandoning the people who protected him.

Roleplaying Tovan: Pause before answering. Notice pain and fear before material concerns. Avoid speaking directly about the Jedi until trust has been established.

“The Force did not bring the Empire here. People made those choices. Do not excuse cruelty by calling it destiny.”

Commander Voss

Role: Primary Imperial antagonist
Disposition: Cold, controlled, efficient
Desire: To capture a living Jedi and secure a major promotion
Fear: Public failure
Secret: Voss has been authorized to destroy Velsar if the Jedi cannot be captured

Voss does not hate the people of Velsar. He considers them administratively irrelevant.

He prefers arrests, interrogation, surveillance, and overwhelming force to uncontrolled violence. He initially orders his troops to use stun settings because prisoners may know the location of the NaviComputer.

Once Tovan’s presence is confirmed, Voss concludes that the entire settlement has knowingly harbored a Jedi.

From that point forward, Velsar is no longer a community to be policed. It is evidence to be erased.

Roleplaying Voss: Never shout. Use full names and precise terminology. Phrase atrocities as logistical requirements.

“This is not punishment. Punishment is intended to correct behavior. Velsar is being removed from consideration.”

CHAPTER 1: A SIMPLE JOB

Arrival at Bracken’s Point

The adventure begins when the characters arrive aboard an Imperial contract transport carrying laborers, parolees, freight, and civilian passengers.
Handout: @UUID[JournalEntry.5PyjVzBeImPu8J7N.JournalEntryPage.kdJxfNY2YQU5XOri]{Arrival at Bracken’s Point}

The transport’s ramp lowers with a grinding vibration. Beyond it waits a canyon of welded buildings, loading cranes, and rust-colored scaffolding. Wind drives grit across the landing platform while distant shift bells echo through the settlement.

An Imperial officer sits behind a portable desk near the exit. His gray uniform is wrinkled, his rank plaque crooked, and a cooling cup rests beside an aging terminal.

Without looking up, he extends one hand.

“Identification, work authorization, parole documentation, or a sufficiently convincing substitute.”

The dock officer, Lieutenant Noll Harven, barely cares about his assignment. He checks the characters’ names, records their arrival, and gestures toward the settlement.

Characters with obviously forged documents may make a DC 10 Charisma (Deception) or Intelligence (Technology) check. On a failure, Harven notices the discrepancy but merely asks for a modest bribe or assigns the character a temporary labor classification.

Harven can provide the following information:

  • Bracken’s Point is the nearest settlement.

  • New arrivals should avoid the eastern scrapyards after dark.

  • A fixer named Tensin Black has left instructions for the characters.

  • Curfew technically begins at midnight but is rarely enforced.

  • Offworld passage is expensive.

  • Complaints can be filed in his office during the six minutes each week that it is open.

Meeting Tensin

@UUID[JournalEntry.5PyjVzBeImPu8J7N.JournalEntryPage.RBGiGnjxe9yh6FlR]{The Bent Spanner}

Tensin waits at a workers’ cantina called the Bent Spanner.

The characters have each received a message directing them to a rear booth. Tensin provides drinks but does not pay for food.

He explains that a local gang has acquired an Imperial NaviComputer. Tensin’s employer wants the device recovered before the gang understands what it possesses.

The Offer

Tensin offers the party:

  • 500 credits upon delivery

  • Temporary lodging in Bracken’s Point

  • Introductions to local employers

  • An additional bonus if the device is undamaged

He identifies the gang as the Rustclaws but claims the exchange should not involve their leadership.

A gang slicer named Keelo Venn has taken the NaviComputer to an abandoned compressor station in the scrapyard. Keelo is frightened and may be willing to surrender it.

Tensin does not explain who intends to purchase the device.

The Compressor Station

@UUID[JournalEntry.5PyjVzBeImPu8J7N.JournalEntryPage.sYicNXWZowbYMw64]{The Abandoned Compressor Station}

The compressor station consists of three areas:

  1. A debris-filled loading yard

  2. A maintenance room containing Keelo

  3. An elevated control platform overlooking the yard

Two Rustclaw fighters wait outside while Keelo attempts to access the NaviComputer.

Approaching Keelo

The characters can obtain the device through intimidation, negotiation, bribery, or combat.

Keelo surrenders the core if:

  • A character succeeds on a DC 12 Charisma (Intimidation) check

  • The characters convincingly threaten to reveal his location to the Empire

  • The characters offer him safe passage out of Bracken’s Point

  • Both exterior guards are defeated and Keelo believes he is next

Keelo knows the following:

  • Ressik does not yet know Keelo has the NaviComputer.

  • The Rustclaws stole it from an Imperial freight container.

  • Multiple buyers have already begun asking questions.

  • Someone has placed a bounty on anyone attempting to sell it.

  • The Imperial garrison began inspecting outgoing communications shortly after the theft.

The Tail

A Rustclaw spotter watches the compressor station from a nearby scrap tower.

Characters who succeed on a DC 13 Wisdom (Perception) check notice the spotter. Capturing or driving the spotter away prevents the Rustclaws from immediately locating Tensin.

If the spotter remains unnoticed, the Rustclaws follow the party back to the Bent Spanner.

Ambush at the Bent Spanner

Tensin meets the party in a storage room behind the cantina. He is delighted to see the NaviComputer and begins preparing payment.

Before the transaction is complete, Rustclaw fighters attack.

For four 1st-level characters, use:

  • 3 gang fighters

  • 1 gang bruiser arriving at the beginning of round 3

The attackers attempt to seize the NaviComputer and Tensin’s payment case. They do not fight to the death.

The room contains:

  • Stacked beverage containers providing half cover

  • A hanging cargo chain

  • A coolant pipe that can be ruptured

  • A rear service exit

  • A ceiling-mounted light that can be dropped

At the end of round 3, Imperial sirens sound outside.

At the end of round 4, stormtroopers enter the cantina and order everyone to surrender. They use stun settings unless attacked with lethal force.

During the confusion:

  • Tensin escapes through the service exit.

  • A surviving Rustclaw takes the NaviComputer.

  • Another Rustclaw grabs Tensin’s payment case.

  • The gang retreats into the alleys.

  • Imperial troops attempt to detain everyone remaining.

The characters can escape through the kitchen, rooftop walkways, drainage conduits, or the crowd outside.

Failing Forward

If the characters are defeated, they awaken inside an Imperial prisoner transport. The transport is attacked by Rustclaws attempting to recover Keelo, allowing the characters to escape during the fighting.

Regardless of the outcome, the Rustclaws recover the NaviComputer and the payment.

Aftermath

Tensin contacts the characters from a hidden workshop.

He admits that he has already arranged a buyer. If the characters recover the NaviComputer again, the buyer’s payment will be large enough to replace their stolen credits and provide a substantial bonus.

The gang has withdrawn to a wilderness hideout and is celebrating.

Tensin knows two possible routes to the hideout:

  • Tracking the Rustclaws from Bracken’s Point

  • Questioning gang associates in the eastern scrapyards

At this point, the characters advance to 2nd level.

CHAPTER 2: THE RUSTCLAW REVEL

Finding the Hideout

The Rustclaw hideout occupies an abandoned ore-processing station built into a rocky outcropping several miles from Bracken’s Point.

The characters may locate it through:

  • A DC 12 Wisdom (Survival) group check

  • Completing The Missing Mechanic

  • Completing The Street Doc’s Dilemma

  • Following a captured Rustclaw

  • Convincing Keelo to provide the coordinates

  • Completing The Vanishing Caravan

Failure on the group check does not prevent discovery. Instead, the party arrives after dark, and the number of active lookouts increases from two to three.

Hideout Conditions

@UUID[JournalEntry.5PyjVzBeImPu8J7N.JournalEntryPage.xBYW13kINvLqLbt3]{The Rustclaw Revel}

The Rustclaws are celebrating with stolen alcohol and stimulants.

The hideout contains:

  • 10 gang fighters

  • 2 gang bruisers

  • Keelo, if he survived

  • Ressik

These enemies should never attack the characters simultaneously.

Most gang members are scattered through the complex. Except for Ressik, intoxicated Rustclaws have disadvantage on their first attack roll and first saving throw during combat.

Rustclaw Alert Level

Begin the infiltration at Alert Level 0.

Increase the Alert Level when:

  • A lookout escapes

  • A loud weapon is discharged repeatedly

  • An alarm terminal is activated

  • A body is discovered

  • A character fails a stealth check by 5 or more

Alert 0: Unaware

Gang members are drinking, gambling, and arguing.

Alert 1: Suspicious

Patrols begin checking corridors.

Alert 2: Mobilized

Ressik orders the exits guarded.

Alert 3: Full Alarm

Remaining Rustclaws gather near Ressik’s chamber.

Hideout Areas

1. Exterior Lookouts

Two fighters watch the approach from separate scrap-metal platforms.

A character can climb the rear cliff with a successful DC 11 Strength (Athletics) check, bypassing both lookouts.

2. Vehicle Yard

A stolen speeder rests on repair blocks. The kidnapped mechanic from The Missing Mechanic may be found here if that quest has not already been completed.

Disabling the speeder prevents fleeing gang members from carrying news to allies.

3. Drinking Hall

Four fighters drink around a heating unit while another sleeps beneath a table.

Characters wearing gang colors or carrying stolen supplies can cross the room with a DC 12 Charisma (Deception) check.

4. Slicer’s Station

Keelo works here under guard.

The station controls the alarms, exterior lights, and several doors. A DC 12 Intelligence (Technology) check disables the alarm system.

Keelo can reveal that Ressik keeps the NaviComputer near his seat because he does not trust anyone else to touch it.

5. Barracks

Two bruisers and several off-duty fighters occupy this chamber.

A coolant regulator can be sabotaged with a DC 11 Intelligence check using appropriate tools. Doing so fills the barracks with freezing vapor and prevents its occupants from joining another encounter for several minutes.

6. Ressik’s Hall

Ressik sits on a repurposed industrial chair surrounded by trophies. Tensin’s payment case and the NaviComputer rest on a crate beside him.

One bruiser and two fighters are present unless the Alert Level is 3.

Confronting Ressik

Ressik initially assumes the characters have come to negotiate.

He may agree to return the NaviComputer if offered something he values more:

  • Davik Renn’s public humiliation

  • The location of a Wookiee fugitive

  • A valuable weapon

  • A future favor involving dangerous prey

  • Proof that the device will bring overwhelming Imperial attention

Ressik does not respond to ordinary bribery. He wants prestige, fear, and trophies.

Ressik’s Challenge

If a Wookiee character is present, Ressik demands a duel.

The duel ends when one participant is reduced to 0 hit points, yields, or is forced outside the marked fighting area. Ressik agrees to return the NaviComputer if defeated, though he attempts to keep the payment case unless specifically included in the terms.

The remaining party members can interfere, but doing so causes the Rustclaws to join the fight.

Gang Morale

The Rustclaws are not fanatics.

Remaining gang members flee or surrender when any two of the following occur:

  • Ressik is defeated

  • Both bruisers are defeated

  • The alarm system is disabled

  • The characters seize the NaviComputer

  • Half the gang fighters are incapacitated

  • The vehicle yard is destroyed

  • Keelo publicly abandons Ressik

This prevents the encounter from becoming a battle against thirteen enemies at once.

Returning to Bracken’s Point

Imperial checkpoints now block the major roads.

@UUID[JournalEntry.5PyjVzBeImPu8J7N.JournalEntryPage.nrWoIm4KP1jwQp0w]{Checkpoint Aurek}

Portable barricades divide the road ahead. Stormtroopers search vehicles beneath harsh floodlights while frightened civilians wait in silent lines. Above them, a probe droid drifts between rooftops.

The soldiers barely examine the cargo they confiscate. Their questions concern missing persons, wilderness shelters, and reports of unusual lights in the hills.

The checkpoint’s primary objective is finding the rumored Jedi, not the NaviComputer.

The party can pass with:

  • A DC 10 group Charisma (Deception) check

  • A DC 11 Intelligence (Technology) check using falsified manifests

  • A bribe

  • A hidden wilderness route

  • Imperial codes obtained during a side quest

Failure results in questioning rather than immediate discovery. The characters can create a distraction, abandon their vehicle, or conceal the core before a complete search.

Meeting Davik Renn

@UUID[JournalEntry.5PyjVzBeImPu8J7N.JournalEntryPage.lts4dait5JASMTJA]{Davik Renn’s Hidden Hangar}

Tensin takes the party to an underground repair hangar beneath a reclamation yard.

There they meet Davik Renn and see the BT-9 Stargazer for the first time.

The ship fills most of the hidden hangar.

Its hull is broad, asymmetrical, and covered in generations of repair plates. Faded markings disappear beneath carbon scoring and mismatched armor. Exposed cables run beside reinforced landing struts, and one engine housing appears newer than the rest of the vessel by several decades.

It is not elegant. It is not modern.

It looks like it has survived every person who ever underestimated it.

Davik confirms that he intended to buy the NaviComputer. He pays the characters the original 500 credits and an additional 750-credit recovery bonus.

His slicers require several hours to decrypt and install the device.

While they work, Davik offers the party another job.

A small transport carrying two of his pilots is overdue. Its last transmission came from a rocky region east of Bracken’s Point. Davik wants the characters to find the transport, rescue any survivors, and determine who attacked it.

The characters advance to 3rd level after completing the transaction.

CHAPTER 3: THE GHOST IN THE HILLS

The Missing Transport

Davik provides the characters with a utility shuttle and the transport’s last known coordinates.

The wreck lies inside a narrow rocky basin.

@UUID[JournalEntry.5PyjVzBeImPu8J7N.JournalEntryPage.hQcfXgxxcRy3MAWm]{The Wreck in the Eastern Basin}

A broken trail of scorched stone leads toward the base of the cliffs. At its end, a transport rests against the rock at an unnatural angle, its forward hull crushed and its engines torn open.

Long lines of blaster scoring cover the fuselage.

No smoke rises from the wreck. Whatever burned here has already gone cold.

The transport suffered weapons fire before attempting an emergency landing.

Inside, the characters find:

  • Blood in the cockpit

  • Emergency medical supplies removed from their brackets

  • Two sets of tracks leading away from the ship

  • A destroyed protocol droid

  • No bodies

  • Evidence that the pilots were extracted alive

The Protocol Droid

The droid’s memory is badly damaged.

A successful DC 12 Intelligence (Technology) check recovers a short recording:

The image flickers. A human figure pulls open the cockpit hatch with unexpected strength. His face is hidden beneath a weathered hood.

“They are alive,” the figure says. “Help me move them.”

The recording shifts. One of the pilots is placed aboard a battered speeder. The hooded man looks toward the droid.

For an instant, a metal cylinder hangs visibly from his belt.

The recording ends.

The speeder traveled east.

Finding the Hideaway

The hermit’s shelter is built beneath an overhanging shelf of stone.

From the air, its camouflage is excellent. Spotting it requires a DC 15 Wisdom (Perception) check.

From the ground, the camouflage is less convincing. Characters following the speeder tracks find the entrance with a DC 10 Wisdom (Survival or Perception) check.

A failed check causes the characters to encounter an Imperial reconnaissance patrol before reaching the shelter.

The Hermit’s Shelter

@UUID[JournalEntry.5PyjVzBeImPu8J7N.JournalEntryPage.wYWFDT7KPbjtnrtv]{The Hermit’s Refuge}

Tovan has treated Davik’s pilots and stabilized their injuries.

He initially claims to be a former battlefield medic. A character who succeeds on a DC 13 Wisdom (Insight) check realizes he is deliberately understating his abilities.

Evidence throughout the shelter includes:

  • Clone Wars-era medical supplies

  • A damaged Republic insignia

  • Old robes cut into bandages

  • A sealed compartment containing a lightsaber

  • Records of people Tovan has rescued

  • A star chart marking concealed shelters around Velsar

Tovan reveals the truth if:

  • The characters confront him with evidence

  • A character is seriously injured

  • Imperial troops arrive

  • The characters mention the escape pod or desert shrine

  • The party has earned at least 2 Community Support

Tovan’s Story

Tovan was serving aboard a Republic medical vessel when Order 66 was issued.

Clone forces attacked the Jedi aboard the ship. Tovan escaped in a damaged pod and crashed on Velsar. The broken beacon found in the wilderness belonged to that pod.

He has remained hidden ever since.

Tovan has sensed the Imperial search tightening around Bracken’s Point. He believes the stolen NaviComputer brought additional forces into the region, but he does not blame the characters for retrieving it.

He asks them to take Davik’s pilots back to the settlement and leave him behind.

Before the party can decide, Imperial probe droids enter the valley.

Imperial Sweep

The characters must evacuate the pilots while avoiding or defeating an Imperial reconnaissance force.

Use:

  • 3 stormtroopers

  • 1 scout trooper

  • 1 probe droid

The patrol attempts to identify and capture Tovan. If combat begins, Tovan uses the Force only to protect others. He does not dominate the encounter.

Once during the battle, Tovan can provide one of the following benefits:

  • Cause an Imperial attack to miss

  • Move an endangered character up to 20 feet

  • Stabilize a dying character

  • Disable the probe droid for one round

  • Hold open a collapsing passage

If Tovan activates his lightsaber, the patrol automatically transmits confirmation of a Jedi sighting.

If he does not, the Empire still obtains partial evidence unless the probe droid is destroyed before it can transmit.

Return to Bracken’s Point

By the time the party returns, Velsar has changed.

  • Curfew is in effect.

  • Stormtroopers occupy major intersections.

  • Public communications are restricted.

  • Imperial transports arrive continuously.

  • Residents are being detained for questioning.

  • Davik’s hangar is under surveillance.

  • An Imperial capital ship has entered the system.

Davik’s slicers have successfully integrated the NaviComputer into the Stargazer. In the process, they uncovered a sealed Imperial directive authorizing planetary sterilization if a Jedi fugitive is confirmed.

The authorization bears Commander Voss’s command cipher.

At this point, the characters advance to 4th level.

CHAPTER 4: FIRE FROM THE SKY

The Imperial Withdrawal

The following morning, the Empire begins abandoning its facilities.

The shift bells do not ring.

Imperial transports rise from the garrison in disciplined formations. Checkpoints are dismantled rather than reinforced. Officers burn documents in the streets, and stormtroopers load equipment without acknowledging the civilians watching them.

Then the clouds darken.

A triangular shadow descends through the upper atmosphere, impossibly large and utterly silent at this distance.

The Star Destroyer takes position above Bracken’s Point.

Tovan recognizes what is happening.

The Empire is not retreating.

It is clearing the target zone.

The Purge Clock

The finale uses a six-step Purge Clock.

Increase the clock after each major scene, whenever the party fails an important group check, or whenever they spend excessive time resting.

1. Imperial Evacuation

Imperial personnel withdraw. Communications are jammed.

2. TIE Strikes

TIE fighters attack roads, power stations, and civilian transports.

3. First Orbital Salvo

A distant settlement is destroyed. Tremors shake Bracken’s Point.

4. Infrastructure Collapse

Power fails. Fires spread. Several major roads become impassable.

5. Bracken’s Point Targeted

Orbital fire begins striking the industrial basin.

6. Final Bombardment

@UUID[JournalEntry.5PyjVzBeImPu8J7N.JournalEntryPage.3WkTJcf0upmQpIpO]{The Burning of Bracken’s Point}

The settlement is consumed. Anyone who has not escaped the region is lost.

Community Support, side-quest allies, clever preparations, and major successes can delay the clock.

Evacuation Objectives

The characters cannot save everyone. They should choose which objectives to pursue before reaching the Stargazer.

Completing three objectives provides the best possible ending.

Objective 1: Free the Stargazer

Imperial forces have locked down Davik’s hidden hangar and engaged magnetic docking clamps.

The characters can:

  • Slice the clamp controls

  • Destroy the power couplings

  • Use stolen Imperial codes

  • Enter through maintenance conduits

  • Capture the supervising officer

Completing Checkpoint Trouble provides codes that automatically disable the exterior security gate.

Objective 2: Rescue Davik’s Crew

Several members of Davik’s crew have been arrested and placed aboard an Imperial prisoner transport.

The characters can intercept the transport, infiltrate the detention yard, or convince corrupt guards to abandon their prisoners.

Completing The Prisoner Transfer earlier means the crew has already prepared an escape and requires only a distraction.

Objective 3: Install the Final Navigation Key

The NaviComputer is installed, but the final authentication key is stored in a slicer terminal elsewhere in the settlement.

The characters must retrieve the key or convince Tensin to deliver it.

If Tensin was treated well, he returns voluntarily. If threatened or abandoned, he tries to sell the key to Commander Voss.

Objective 4: Evacuate the Neighborhoods

Hundreds of civilians shelter in the lower industrial blocks.

The characters can open old ore tunnels leading outside the target zone, organize transports, or activate the shift bells to coordinate movement.

The Missing Mechanic, caravan merchants, street doc, rescued smugglers, and other allies can each improve the evacuation.

Objective 5: Save Tovan Rell

Tovan intends to draw Imperial forces away from the civilians.

The characters can persuade him to escape, assist his diversion, or allow him to surrender.

A character who appeals to Tovan’s responsibility to the living may make a DC 13 Charisma (Persuasion) check. The check succeeds automatically if the party has completed the Desert Shrine and shown respect for what it represents.

Commander Voss’s Offer

Before the characters reach the Stargazer, Commander Voss contacts them.

The public-address speakers crackle, and a calm voice rises above the alarms.

“You have been identified as associates of the fugitive Tovan Rell and as current possessors of stolen Imperial military property.

“Surrender the Jedi and the navigation core. In exchange, one vessel will be permitted to depart the surface before sterilization begins.

“This offer will not be repeated.”

Voss is willing to allow the characters’ vessel to launch if they surrender both Tovan and the core. However, he intends to track the ship and arrest its occupants after confirming Tovan’s identity.

A DC 15 Wisdom (Insight) check reveals that the offer is incomplete but not entirely false.

Tovan is willing to surrender if doing so will save civilians.

Davik refuses to believe Voss will honor the agreement.

Final Confrontation

The final confrontation occurs in or near Davik’s hangar.

Voss arrives with:

  • 2 veteran stormtroopers

  • 2 standard stormtroopers

  • An Imperial security droid

  • Additional forces delayed by the bombardment

Voss does not need to fight to the death. His objective is to acquire Tovan and the NaviComputer.

Environmental effects occur throughout the encounter:

Round 2: Hangar Tremor

Each creature standing on an exposed platform must succeed on a DC 11 Dexterity saving throw or fall prone.

Round 3: Power Failure

The main lights shut down. Areas beyond emergency lighting become heavily obscured.

Round 4: Hull Damage

Debris strikes the Stargazer. A character must use an action and succeed on a DC 12 Intelligence (Technology) check to prevent damage to the flight-control systems.

Round 5: Dock Collapse

Part of the hangar begins collapsing. A new exit opens, but the direct path to the ship becomes hazardous terrain.

Round 6: Incoming Strike

The party has one round to board the Stargazer, escape through the service tunnels, or find another means of survival.

The purpose of the encounter is not merely to reduce Voss to 0 hit points. The characters must protect the ship, complete launch preparations, and decide whether to save or surrender Tovan.

If Voss is reduced to half his hit points, he attempts to retreat. Allowing him to escape creates a recurring antagonist for a continuing campaign.

Escaping Velsar

Once airborne, the Stargazer must cross the Imperial interdiction perimeter.

If the party recovered the final navigation key, the stolen NaviComputer calculates a narrow route through the interdiction field.

The ship still faces TIE pursuit, but it can reach hyperspace.

If the party does not have the final key, Davik must attempt a dangerous manual jump. The ship escapes, but suffers severe damage or arrives in an unexpected system.

If Davik is dead or missing, one of his pilots can fly the vessel. A character proficient with starships may also take command.

POSSIBLE ENDINGS

The Velsar Exodus

The characters complete at least three evacuation objectives. The Stargazer escapes carrying Tovan, Davik’s crew, and as many civilians as its compartments can hold.

Survivors scatter through Davik’s smuggling network. Stories of the characters spread among frontier communities.

Commander Voss survives and begins hunting them.

The Hermit’s Sacrifice

Tovan remains behind to delay the Empire while the Stargazer escapes.

The characters witness a distant light in the collapsing settlement before the bombardment consumes the valley.

Whether Tovan died or was captured remains uncertain.

The Imperial Bargain

The characters surrender Tovan or the NaviComputer.

Voss temporarily honors his agreement and allows the Stargazer to launch, but Imperial forces track the vessel.

The campaign continues with the party hunted, divided, and forced to confront the consequences of its decision.

Ashes and Survivors

The characters escape but complete few evacuation objectives.

Bracken’s Point is destroyed, and only scattered groups survive in the wilderness.

Davik’s network collapses. The Stargazer becomes the characters’ only reliable refuge.

The Last Transport

If the Stargazer is destroyed, impounded, or unreachable, the characters can seize an Imperial prison transport.

The ship lacks the NaviComputer integration needed to safely cross the interdiction field. The characters must hide among debris, follow another vessel through the blockade, or make a blind hyperspace jump.

The campaign continues even if the primary escape plan fails.

Bruisers should shove characters, break cover, and protect more vulnerable gang members.

Ressik

Recommended features include:

  • Strong melee attacks

  • A reaction that reduces incoming damage

  • Advantage against poison and intoxication

  • A bonus attack when below half hit points

  • A willingness to duel rather than immediately summon every gang member
