CONTINUING THE CAMPAIGN

At the end of Ashes of Velsar, the characters possess or serve aboard the BT-9 Stargazer.

If Davik survives, he becomes their patron and captain. His larger syndicate expects him to explain the loss of Velsar, the stolen Imperial technology, and the refugees now occupying his ship.

If Davik dies, the characters inherit the Stargazer in practice, though his creditors, syndicate superiors, and former partners may dispute their ownership.

Commander Voss may continue pursuing the party, particularly if they escaped with Tovan or the NaviComputer.

Possible future adventures include:

  • Finding sanctuary for Velsar’s refugees

  • Repairing the damaged Stargazer

  • Breaking an Imperial tracking signal

  • Rescuing Tovan from an Imperial prison

  • Exposing Voss’s purge order

  • Repaying Davik’s syndicate obligations

  • Smuggling supplies to other occupied worlds

  • Discovering why the Imperial NaviComputer contained routes to a classified system

Chapter 1: A Simple Job

This revised chapter preserves the original premise while removing the forced-loss sequence. The characters’ choices determine whether the Rustclaws steal the NaviComputer, whether Tensin is captured, and how quickly the Empire identifies the party.

The essential revelation is that the NaviComputer consists of two components:

  • The IN-4 navigation core, currently held by Keelo Venn.

  • A removable Imperial authentication wafer, already taken to Ressik’s hideout.

The core cannot bypass an interdiction field without the wafer. This ensures the characters have a reason to confront Ressik even if they completely defeat the Rustclaw ambush.

Chapter Overview

The characters:

  1. Arrive at Bracken’s Point.

  2. Pass through Lieutenant Harven’s indifferent processing station.

  3. Meet Tensin Black at the Bent Spanner.

  4. Travel to the abandoned compressor station.

  5. Recover the IN-4 core from Keelo Venn.

  6. Discover or evade a Rustclaw tail.

  7. Return to Tensin for payment.

  8. Survive a Rustclaw ambush and Imperial intervention.

  9. Learn that the authentication wafer is at Ressik’s hideout.

  10. Advance to 2nd level.

1. Arrival on Velsar

The characters arrive aboard the Wayward Sun, an aging Imperial contract transport carrying laborers, parolees, freight handlers, and passengers unable to afford better passage.

Each character was contacted separately by Tensin Black and offered work upon arrival. They do not need to know one another before the adventure.

Arrival Boxed Text

The transport descends through a haze of industrial smoke and windblown dust.

Below, Bracken’s Point fills a broad rocky basin. Landing pads, scrapyards, furnaces, and densely packed buildings spread beneath webs of catwalks and power cables. Beyond the perimeter walls, rough roads disappear between broken ridges and abandoned excavation cuts.

The transport lands with a violent shudder.

A warning tone sounds, the cargo ramp lowers, and hot metallic air rolls into the passenger compartment. Outside, workers guide freight sleds between battered starships while an Imperial officer waits behind a portable processing desk.

He does not appear pleased to see any of you.

Give the players time to describe their characters and explain why each has come to Velsar.

Possible reasons include employment, exile, debt, forged travel documents, release from Imperial custody, smuggling contacts, or a desire to disappear.

2. Lieutenant Noll Harven

Lieutenant Noll Harven processes arrivals beside the landing pad. His uniform is wrinkled, his terminal outdated, and his attention divided between passenger records and a cooling cup of caf.

Harven is not secretly benevolent. He is simply underpaid, bored, and unwilling to create additional work for himself.

Harven Boxed Text

The officer gestures without looking up.

“Identification. Employment authorization. Parole documentation. Cargo declarations.”

He pauses and finally glances toward the line.

“Or something close enough that I can pretend I received them.”

Characters with legitimate documents pass without difficulty.

A character using forged, expired, or questionable documents may make one of the following checks:

  • DC 10 Charisma (Deception): Confidently explain the discrepancy.

  • DC 10 Intelligence (Technology): Correct or obscure the faulty record.

  • DC 8 Charisma (Persuasion): Convince Harven the problem is not worth investigating.

  • 50-credit bribe: Harven marks the paperwork as temporarily approved.

Failed Check

Harven notices the problem but does not arrest the character. Instead, choose one consequence:

  • The character is registered as a temporary industrial laborer.

  • Harven confiscates 50 credits as a “processing penalty.”

  • The character’s name is marked for a future records review.

  • Harven directs the character to report for a work assignment the following morning.

This introduces complications without preventing the adventure.

What Harven Knows

Harven can provide the following information:

  • Bracken’s Point is the largest settlement on Velsar.

  • The eastern scrapyards are controlled by local gangs.

  • A fixer named Tensin Black left instructions for the characters.

  • The Bent Spanner is located near Market Row.

  • Offworld passage is expensive.

  • The local Imperial presence is normally small and poorly supplied.

  • Several unusual freight inspections began earlier that morning.

Harven does not yet know about the NaviComputer theft.

3. First Impressions

The characters receive an automated message from Tensin directing them to meet at the Bent Spanner near the evening shift bell.

They have approximately one hour to explore.

Use this period to introduce Bracken’s Point through one brief scene.

Market Dispute

A cargo hauler has broken down in the center of Market Row. Workers struggle to move it while merchants argue about the blocked street.

A character can help with:

  • DC 10 Strength (Athletics): Shift the damaged hauler.

  • DC 10 Intelligence (Technology): Restart its repulsor system.

  • DC 10 Charisma (Persuasion): Organize the workers.

Success earns the party its first favorable reputation among the locals. One worker recognizes them later and provides directions or a warning about the Rustclaws.

Failure causes no serious consequence, but the characters arrive at the Bent Spanner covered in grease, dust, or coolant.

4. The Bent Spanner

The Bent Spanner is a crowded workers’ cantina near the boundary between Market Row and the Freight Quarter.

Cantina Boxed Text

Heat, machinery noise, and overlapping conversation fill the cantina.

Mechanics sit beside freight crews in oil-stained work clothes. A battered service droid carries dented cups between tables while an alien musician tunes an instrument near a low wooden stage.

Near the rear wall, a dark-haired man in a long coat sits alone in a booth with a clear view of the front entrance, kitchen door, and loading alley.

He raises two fingers when he sees you.

“You must be the professionals.”

The man is Tensin Black.

Tensin’s Offer

Tensin explains that a Rustclaw slicer named Keelo Venn has possession of stolen Imperial navigation hardware.

Keelo is hiding in an abandoned compressor station inside the eastern scrapyards. Tensin wants the characters to acquire the device and return it intact.

Tensin offers:

  • 100 credits per character in advance

  • 500 credits total upon delivery

  • Temporary lodging for two nights

  • An introduction to his buyer if the job is completed cleanly

Tensin supplies a simple scanner capable of identifying the device.

What Tensin Reveals

Tensin truthfully explains:

  • The Rustclaws stole the device from an Imperial freight container.

  • Keelo has tried to sell it without Ressik’s permission.

  • Keelo is frightened of both Ressik and the Empire.

  • Tensin’s buyer will pay far more than the Rustclaws understand.

Tensin conceals:

  • The buyer is Davik Renn.

  • Tensin already promised Davik he could obtain the device.

  • Tensin does not know that the authentication wafer has been removed.

  • The stolen core contains an Imperial tamper beacon.

Reading Tensin

A character who succeeds on a DC 12 Wisdom (Insight) check realizes Tensin is withholding the buyer’s identity and is under considerable pressure.

Tensin admits only that his buyer is “someone with a ship and enough enemies to need better navigation.”

5. Reaching the Compressor Station

The abandoned compressor station lies approximately thirty minutes from the cantina.

The characters can travel openly through the scrapyards or move through narrow salvage lanes to avoid attention.

Scrapyard Travel

One character leads a group check using either:

  • DC 10 Wisdom (Survival)

  • DC 10 Intelligence (Investigation)

  • DC 11 Dexterity (Stealth)

On a success, the party reaches the station without being observed.

On a failure, a Rustclaw spotter notices them. This does not immediately trigger combat, but it gives the gang an advantage during the later ambush.

6. The Abandoned Compressor Station

Use the Abandoned Compressor Station and Eastern Scrapyard battlemap.

The station consists of an exterior salvage yard, a raised maintenance building, and a lower control platform.

Occupants

  • Keelo Venn

  • Two Rustclaw fighters

  • One distant Rustclaw spotter, if the group failed the travel check

The fighters believe they are guarding Keelo from rival gangs. They do not know he intends to betray Ressik.

Exterior Boxed Text

A rusted compressor tower rises above walls of stacked machinery.

Two armed figures occupy the yard below. One leans against a cargo container while the other watches the surrounding scrap lanes from a raised platform.

Blue light flickers through the station windows. Inside, someone is working quickly at an overloaded terminal.

Dealing with the Guards

The characters may fight, deceive, bribe, or bypass the guards.

Possible approaches include:

  • Claiming to be buyers with a DC 11 Charisma (Deception) check.

  • Bribing the guards with at least 50 credits.

  • Creating a distraction with a DC 11 Technology or Sleight of Hand check.

  • Sneaking through the damaged western fence with a DC 10 Dexterity (Stealth) group check.

  • Defeating the guards in combat.

The guards flee if one is incapacitated and the other is reduced below half hit points.

7. Keelo Venn

Keelo is inside the maintenance room attempting to access the IN-4 navigation core.

He is exhausted, frightened, and increasingly convinced Ressik intends to kill him.

Keelo Boxed Text

A young man crouches over an open equipment case filled with cables, slicing tools, and improvised power cells.

Inside the case rests a reinforced black cylinder covered in Imperial seals.

The man freezes when he sees you.

“Before anyone starts shooting, I would like to point out that the Empire wants this thing more than any of us do.”

Keelo’s Attitude

Keelo begins hostile but frightened. He wants protection and a way out of Bracken’s Point.

He surrenders the navigation core if:

  • A character succeeds on a DC 12 Charisma (Intimidation) check.

  • The party offers him safe passage.

  • The characters reveal that the Rustclaws know his location.

  • Both guards have been defeated.

  • The characters offer at least 100 credits.

A failed social check causes Keelo to trigger a local alarm and move behind cover. He still negotiates once the characters demonstrate they can reach him.

The Missing Wafer

Keelo removed the core’s authentication wafer shortly after the theft. Ressik confiscated it and took it to the Rustclaw hideout.

Without the wafer, the core:

  • Cannot decrypt Imperial interdiction telemetry.

  • Cannot produce valid military navigation credentials.

  • Cannot perform the escape route Davik requires.

  • Remains valuable but is not operational.

Keelo reveals this immediately if treated reasonably. If threatened, he withholds the information until Tensin discovers it later.

The Tamper Beacon

A character examining the core may make a DC 12 Intelligence (Technology) check.

On a success, the character discovers that opening or scanning the device may reactivate an Imperial tamper beacon. The beacon can be disabled with a second DC 12 Technology check.

On a failure, the beacon remains unnoticed.

Disabling it delays the Imperial response during the coming ambush.

8. The Rustclaw Tail

A Rustclaw spotter follows the characters when they leave the compressor station.

The spotter is automatically present if:

  • The characters failed their scrapyard travel check.

  • A guard escaped.

  • Keelo triggered the alarm.

  • The characters openly carried the core through the scrapyards.

A character with passive Perception 13 or higher notices the tail. Otherwise, allow a DC 13 Wisdom (Perception) check.

Confronting the Tail

The characters may:

  • Capture the spotter.

  • Lead the spotter into an ambush.

  • Lose the spotter with a DC 11 group Stealth check.

  • Feed the spotter false information.

  • Change the location of the exchange.

Capturing the spotter reveals that Ressik already knows Keelo tried to sell the device.

If the party eliminates or misdirects the tail, the Rustclaws lose their surprise advantage during the ambush.

9. Returning to Tensin

Tensin waits in a storage room behind the Bent Spanner.

If the characters suspect an ambush, they may insist on meeting somewhere else. Tensin reluctantly agrees to use an adjacent freight warehouse or service tunnel.

Changing locations does not eliminate the confrontation, but it allows the characters to choose more favorable terrain.

Examining the Core

Tensin connects his scanner to the IN-4 core.

If the tamper beacon was not disabled, the scanner reactivates it. A character monitoring the device may notice the transmission with a DC 12 Technology or Perception check.

The transmission can still be interrupted, but the Empire has already narrowed the signal to the district.

Tensin then discovers the missing authentication wafer.

Tensin’s expression changes as lines of red data move across the scanner.

“No. No, that is not what we agreed to.”

He turns the display toward you.

“The core is genuine, but the military authentication wafer is gone. Without it, this is an extremely expensive piece of Imperial scrap.”

He looks toward Keelo, if the slicer is present.

“Where is it?”

Keelo swallows.

“Ressik.”

Tensin pays half the promised completion payment if the party delivered the core. He promises the remainder plus a substantial bonus when they recover the wafer.

10. The Rustclaw Ambush

The Rustclaws strike before the discussion concludes.

Use:

  • Two Rustclaw fighters

  • One Rustclaw bruiser

A third fighter waits outside with an escape speeder but only enters if the party attempts to pursue fleeing gang members.

Ambush Objectives

The Rustclaws are not trying to kill everyone. Their priorities are:

  1. Recover the navigation core.

  2. Seize Tensin’s payment case.

  3. Capture Keelo.

  4. Escape before Imperial forces arrive.

The characters can win without defeating every attacker.

Opening Conditions

If the tail remained undetected, the bruiser begins adjacent to the most accessible exit, and the Rustclaws have advantage on initiative.

If the tail was detected or misdirected, the party cannot be surprised and may choose its starting positions.

Environmental Features

The Bent Spanner or warehouse contains:

  • Cargo crates providing half cover

  • Coolant pipes that can be ruptured

  • Hanging chains

  • A movable freight sled

  • Breakable lights

  • Multiple exits

  • Civilians who panic when combat begins

A character may use an action and make an appropriate DC 10–12 ability check to manipulate an environmental feature.

Examples include dropping cargo, creating smoke, blocking a doorway, or cutting the lights.

Enemy Tactics

The bruiser attempts to grapple or shove whoever carries the core.

The fighters provide covering fire and seize loose objectives. They retreat once they possess either the core or Keelo.

The Rustclaws withdraw if:

  • The bruiser is reduced below half hit points.

  • Both fighters are incapacitated.

  • Imperial sirens are heard.

  • Their escape route is blocked.

  • They acquire the core and can flee.

11. Imperial Intervention

The timing of the Imperial response depends on the party’s actions.

Beacon Disabled

Imperial forces arrive at the end of round 5 or immediately after the Rustclaws retreat.

Beacon Detected but Interrupted

Imperial forces arrive at the end of round 4.

Beacon Active

Imperial forces arrive at the end of round 3.

The response force consists of stormtroopers under orders to use stun settings. Their objective is to arrest witnesses and recover the stolen device.

The adventure continues, but the characters begin Chapter 2 as wanted fugitives.
